areas.verdict: No. The loop is not built yet: Sparkie has no action to read code, edit a part, run the gate or install (heal-3), and the gate cannot pass on Spark 2 at all until the stand-in fleet stops reading the real releases folder and the real /proc/meminfo (sticky-1). Fix first, all small: sticky-1 followed by one full gate run on Spark 2, the lock covering every shipped file (BI-2), the tool-count contradiction (BI-4), and the stale lines in the architecture map (sticky-6). Then build update_console once, carrying heal-3, BI-1's settle window, one update record (sticky-2) and source kept in step (add-3); the other findings are duplicates of these or more than the owner needs.

No, this area is not ready to hand to the Sparks: as built, the gate cannot pass on Spark 2 (real /proc/meminfo and real snapshots leak into the stand-in fleet, service/src/05-library.mjs:52 and 18-workflows.mjs:444), Sparkie has no action to run the gate or the installer, and the installer run from inside the console kills itself at its own restart (deploy/host-on-portal.sh:202) or stops at a /dev/tty prompt (:327). Fix first, in this order: works/gate-1 (gate passes on Linux), sticky-4 (a result file Sparkie can read), works/gate-2 (the lock covers everything shipped), sticky-1 and works/gate-3 with the stub installer test (an install or undo can never leave the console stopped or restore the running build), self-fix/gate-1 (update_console outside the unit) and self-fix/gate-3 (the console says after a restart what happened). Of 27 findings about 10 are distinct and the rest are duplicates of each other or of the unbuilt plan in 01-gap-analysis-plan.md:73-78; the owner still has to decide whether an hour of CPU-only tests on Spark 2 is allowed under the 'nothing but the brain' rule, since Spark 3 and 4 are often off.

Not yet: everyday starts, stops and pair starts are sound, but four confirmed faults should be fixed first, all small: a one-Spark start over a running copy removes the working container and reloads it even when asked for by name on its own Spark (serving-1 with serving-3), the adopt timer writes proven runs that never ran after every install (serving-2), and a brain left stopped or missing has no way back from chat while the failed-switch message says it is back (serving-heal-1 with serving-4). Most of the 'works' findings repeat rows 6 and 14 and Batch A of the earlier analyses that were never built, so the gap is unbuilt backlog, not unknown design. After those four, ship the start-code items in one batch (copy and pull before stops, the two failure rows, images in the workflow version without servePort) with one validation run, and keep two-models-per-Spark parked.

Not ready: for anything that is not an LLM server the console can only watch, so after handoff Sparkie cannot start, restart, keep up, give an address for, or run a script in any service, app or dev box, and an embedding model cannot pass a start (service/src/09-verified.mjs:28-53). Fix four confirmed defects first: the embedding answer test (it sits in locked workflow code, so it is the hardest for Sparkie to do alone), a powered-off Spark's containers reading as running (16-actions.mjs:844-848), the false 'went offline' after every console restart (19-watcher.mjs noteSparkStates never saves), and 'containers: none' when Docker is slow (16-actions.mjs:783-784). Then the owner must answer three questions (keep or retire the editor, may Sparkie set a restart policy on hand-started non-GPU containers on Spark 3/4, is the existing workspace the one data home), after which the adds in order are: files actions, keep_running plus restart_workload with the restart-count watch, workload addresses, then run_script.

Not yet: five small, confirmed things should be fixed first: a chat left "still answering" after a throw during turn setup (14-chats.mjs:212 vs :308), chat and /status dying when the state folder can't be written (14-chats.mjs:24-29, :211), writers that save over desired.json and validations.json after a failed read (20-desired.mjs:9-13, 18-workflows.mjs:78), a daily copy that skips in silence and forgets its record whenever Sparks 3 and 4 are off (25-backup-and-start.mjs:5-9), and an architecture map that states a wrong build, a wrong lock status and a copy exclude list the code does not have (docs/architecture.md:3, :258, :230). All five are S-sized and none needs a new tool; the access.json guard (sticky-1) is the next most useful. After those, the area is sound enough to hand over, and the best additions are the already-planned open-problems list said in chat and /status, a crash record Sparkie can read, reading the audit, and a note with each install snapshot; cut the last-good folder, the per-file restore actions, the STATE_FILES table and the general settings action.

Not yet: three confirmed faults should be fixed first. A Spark whose Docker is not answering reads as "nothing is there" and can make healing stop a healthy part (05-library.mjs:36-39, 19-watcher.mjs:97, 20-heal.mjs:81); one dead recipe source freezes the daily setups look on the same 20 models (11-setups.mjs:197, :233-235); and docs/architecture.md states things that are false today (32 parts, "the tree is not locked", 157 unchecked line numbers) in the page Sparkie reads second. After those, the area is ready once the small additions land: dated notices and a Now line for the brain, look dates on recipe reads, the owner's standing decisions in AGENTS.md, a named-repo route into Recipes, and a note kept with each update; the dark-restart fix is already in the code and needs only its test.

Not yet: three confirmed holes should be closed first, all small. A brain that is stopped rather than hung is never brought back and no chat word can start it (service/src/20-heal.mjs:147, service/src/20-words.mjs:54); a Docker outage on a Spark is read as every container removed and burns a pair's heal tries (service/src/19-watcher.mjs:97, :127, :161-166); and the watchdog is blind to a console that crash-loops at start and never puts back the last build (deploy/host-on-portal.sh:257-262). After those, the area is sound enough to hand over, with the unwatched power cycle (heal-sticky-2), the cut-off start (heal-6), the lingering download container (heal-4) and loop ages on /health (heal-sticky-4) as the next batch, and one read-only check of what exit code a clean power-off really leaves before touching the 255 rule.

Not ready yet: four confirmed faults in /Users/akuppala/Documents/26aiRAG/spark-console/service/src must be fixed first, all small and mostly inside 14-chats.mjs: a chat that locks or returns 500 on a full disk or one unreadable file (BC-S1), a failed or empty reply that loses the next step and tells Telegram the brain is down when it is not (brain-chat-1), "do X, then Y" stalling when X is quick or needed one yes (brain-chat-2), and a stopped or missing brain that nothing brings back and no chat word can start (brain-1). Right behind them, before Sparkie is asked to diagnose or change itself: the per-turn size budget (brain-chat-3), /stop (brain-chat-4), the tool-call probe on a brain swap (BC-S4), the read of its own map and source (brain-3), and approvals that outlive 15 minutes and a restart (brain-add-2). Of 28 findings none was false; 8 are duplicates of others here, and most of the rest hold in a smaller form than proposed, with no new state file except approvals.json and gateway.json.

Not ready yet: three things in the owner's own example ("coding mode") are broken by reading the code, and all three are small. Fix first learning-2 (a second run restarts a model that is already running where the step names it), learning-3 (a step that asks ends the run and no button reaches the chat, so saying it again only asks again) and learning-1 (an 'already-starting' step is not waited on and a long download is called failed at 60 minutes). After those, add the saved names and their `when` line to Sparkie's per-turn record (learn-sticky-4), make the stores honest (learn-sticky-1, -2, -7, learning-heal-6a), and drop the resume, problems.json, `about` notes and history-list proposals as more than the owner needs.

Not yet: four confirmed defects should be fixed first, all small: a carry-on turn can undo an update with no passkey from an internet sign-in (CH-1), Telegram's loop dies for good on one bad read of the secrets file (CH-2), a call to the model address asks Hugging Face and loose-matches names (CH-3), and a throw before the turn's try leaves a chat 'still answering' until a restart (heal-2). With those in, the ways in are sound; the next most useful pieces for a Spark that runs itself are the fault record (heal-1), the last-good access file (sticky-2), the installer's three real calls (heal-3, bash only), keeping promised Telegram result lines (heal-7), and dropping chat routing so the one-brain rule holds in code (heal-5). Of the additions, the owner should decide three: the words /pause and /restart sparkie on Telegram (changes R34), a link and longer life for owner-only buttons, and one standing 'needs me' Telegram line (changes contract 13); /stop with a kept message and speech/image paths should be cut for now.

Not yet: two things should be fixed before handoff. The installer accepts a build whose sign-in is broken because it checks only /health (deploy/host-on-portal.sh:202-227), and the page hides the recovery-code way in when no passkey is on file (service/src/24-handler.mjs:68, public/app.js:5161); the two must-fixes already recorded in 11-api-first-review.json (unlogged handler errors, the owner's API failures pausing agents) belong in the same install. With those in, plus the small hardening kept here (fsync in writePrivate, a last-good copy of access.json, the session gate when no passkey exists, one ways-in check), the area is safe to hand to the Sparks; the gates, per-address limits and recovery codes themselves hold up as written.

Not ready: the gate very likely cannot pass on Spark 2 (the stand-in fleet reads the real /proc/meminfo and releases folder), every install wipes the source tree there, the contract still says Sparkie installs its own updates, and the as-built map and the actions header state things the code does not do. Fix those five first (CD-1, CD-2, CD-S2 smaller, cd-3 with CD-4, and CD-7), all small and mostly docs or a few installer lines; the other 16 findings collapse into about eight small generated-map and lock additions. Even then Sparkie can only read and report on itself (cd-1), because editing, building, testing and installing its own code still wait on the already-planned update_console and change_console, so the owner should not retire the Mac until those exist and have passed the gate on Spark 2 once.

Not ready: the gate cannot pass on Spark 2 today (stand-in Sparks read the real /proc/meminfo and the real releases folder), the real-brain eval has a broken grader and has never been run in full, and Sparkie has no way to run a test or read a result. Fix first works/T1 and works/T2, then build the gate record (tests-add-2), the install and put-back test (works/T3) and the lock that names changed tests and shipped files (works/T4, sticky/T3); the rest is small or can wait. The suite itself is strong on the stand-in fleet, but nothing in it was verified here by running it, and what it never touches (installer, restore, watchdog, real worker, real ssh, the page) is exactly what a self-changing Spark leans on.

Not yet: sign-in, Telegram and status hold up, but four confirmed faults should be fixed first, all in public/app.js plus one small test file. They are: a locked phone loses the answer (works/page-1), a failed send wipes the typed words and shows the browser's raw error (sticky-2), one missed poll marks a running job as failed (works/page-3), and nothing checks that the page even parses before install (works/page-2). After those, the area is ready to hand over; the best addition is a Stop for Sparkie's current turn (add/page-4), and attach, the page-error route, the notices store and the two-step recovery codes should be cut or shrunk as marked.

kept.title: The install calls a build healthy on its first /health answer; one that dies seconds later is never put back
kept.gap: deploy/host-on-portal.sh:215-220 leaves the wait loop at the first answer that names the new build, usually 1-2 s after start. The service's first real work comes later (first watch about 15 s, cable test about 20 s after start), and a throw outside a request ends the process (service/src/25-backup-and-start.mjs:89-92); the unit is Restart=always (host-on-portal.sh:192). The watchdog only acts after 3 missed minutes in a row or state 'failed' (host-on-portal.sh:257-263) and never restores. The stand-in fleet skips real ssh, real worker.py and Tailscale output, so this is exactly the kind of fault the gate passes.
kept.failure: Install a build that throws in a timer on real Spark output 15-20 s after start. Installer prints 'health: ok', swaps the source copy and exits. The console then restarts every ~20 s forever: /health answers most minutes, so the watchdog stays quiet; chats and operations are cut each time; nothing rolls back.
kept.ownerSays: Update yourself, and if the new build doesn't stay up for the first minute, go back by yourself and tell me.
kept.build: In install.sh only: after the first good answer keep polling about 40 s and require the same build and the same startedAt on every sample; otherwise take the existing restore branch (:221-231). Skip the new stub-systemctl harness for now; do one drill by hand before handoff (the 01-plan phase 3 drill 'a crash at start is put back').
guards: Restore keeps using the snapshot's own restore.sh; no new rollback path
Total wait stays under about 90 s so an install is still quick
The stub harness never calls real systemctl or touches the real HOME

kept.title: The 'tested' lock covers 3 files; config.json, catalog.json, worker.py and the whole page install as tested after any edit
kept.gap: The installer compares only the lock's build id, which is server.mjs + dig.mjs + passkey.mjs (deploy/host-on-portal.sh:48, :56-57; service/src/01-setup.mjs:17-21). It ships seven service files and thirteen page files (host-on-portal.sh:20-22). test/lock.mjs:13-17 already computes a fingerprint over every service file but only uses it to detect edits during the run, and does not write it. R29 notes the worker.py case only. The missing piece: config.json can carry `ownerLogin`, which overrides access.json (service/src/03-identity.mjs:43), so an untested config edit can change who the owner is.
kept.failure: Run the gate, then edit service/config.json (a node host, the origin, an ownerLogin) or public/app.js. The build id is unchanged, the installer accepts the lock, and the change goes live with no test run. With a wrong ownerLogin the owner is no longer the owner after the restart.
kept.ownerSays: Nothing installs unless every shipped file is the one the tests ran against.
kept.build: lock.mjs writes `files`: its existing service fingerprint plus a hash of the UI_FILES; add `node test/lock.mjs --check` that recomputes and exits 1 on a mismatch; host-on-portal.sh calls it next to the build-server check (line 24). Separately make the installer refuse a config.json that sets ownerLogin unless it equals the installed access.json owner. Test in test/build.test.mjs: write a lock, change one byte of config.json in a temp copy, expect --check to exit 1.
guards: workflows.lock.json itself stays out of the fingerprint
The BUILD id and /health stay as they are (R30)
An owner-approved config change still installs after a fresh gate run

kept.title: The gate's own command needs Node 21+, the docs say 20, and Spark 2 may have no `node` on PATH
kept.gap: test/lock.mjs:25 passes the literal pattern 'test/*.test.mjs' to `node --test` with no shell; only Node 21+ expands it. test/README.md:15 says 'Node 20 or newer'. The installer accepts Node 18+ and falls back to code-server's bundled Node when `node` is not on PATH (deploy/host-on-portal.sh:76-81), which shows Spark 2 may have none on PATH; AGENTS.md:42-50 writes every step as `node ...`. The fast-gate plan (07, section 5) lists other Spark 2 blockers (real releases folder breaking test/validate.test.mjs:133-136, meminfo) but not this. I could not check Spark 2's version; /health reports it as `node`.
kept.failure: On Spark 2 with Node 20: `node test/lock.mjs` finds no file named 'test/*.test.mjs', exits 1 and prints 'The suite didn’t pass, so nothing was marked as tested' though no test ran. Sparkie would hunt for a failing test that does not exist and could never lock a build.
kept.ownerSays: Run the full gate on Spark 2 and tell me the result.
kept.build: lock.mjs lists the files itself (readdirSync, sorted) and passes them as arguments, refuses to write a lock if fewer files ran than exist, and prints one plain line if Node is older than the version test/README names. The installer's `check` step prints the Node path and version it would use; AGENTS.md names that path for Spark 2. Add `node` version to sparkie_setup's console block. Test in test/build.test.mjs: lock.mjs's file list equals the *.test.mjs files on disk and contains no '*'.
guards: Only lock.mjs writes the lock
Do this together with 07's HOME fix, or the gate still fails on Spark 2 at validate.test.mjs:133
kept.ownerDecision: One read-only check: which Node.js Spark 2 has (GET /health shows `node`). If it is older than 22, the owner installs a newer one; Sparkie must not.

kept.title: Adding one tool requires editing three existing assertions, which the rules forbid
kept.gap: AGENTS.md:47-48 tells the changer to update 'the tool counts in test/change.test.mjs'. Those are literals (test/change.test.mjs:105 `24`, :120 `37`, :142 `24`). AGENTS.md:59 says never edit an existing test to make a change pass, and contract 6.15 (docs/contract.md:408-411) makes any change to an existing assertion wait for the owner's passkey. The exact name lists in test/lib.mjs:40-45 already pin the tool set.
kept.failure: Sparkie adds an action and its name in test/lib.mjs. The gate fails on 24 != 25. It must either break the 'never edit a test' rule or stop; under 6.15 every new tool, however small, needs a passkey tap. A literal-minded local model stalls here.
kept.ownerSays: Add a small read tool for X, test it and show me the change.
kept.build: Replace the three literals with `TOOLS.length + 1` and `ALL_TOOLS.length + 1` (the +1 is ask_sparkie) and keep the name lists exact. Add one line to AGENTS.md: adding a name to TOOLS or CHANGE_TOOLS is the allowed edit; removing or renaming one is not. No new test needed: the door tests already compare the lists exactly, so a tool missing from the list still fails.
guards: The lists stay literal arrays; never derive them from the service
Removing a name from a list still counts as weakening a test

kept.title: 'Test the changes' put-back reports a failure when nothing failed, and strands models when its own stop fails
kept.gap: The put-back loop restarts every container that was running before, stopped or not (service/src/18-workflows.mjs:343, :352-357). For one still running, restart_model returns `{outcome:'already', note:'<c> is running.'}` (service/src/17-changes.mjs:638), which has no operation, so the log line is 'Couldn’t start <c> again: <c> is running.' If the test's own stop_model step throws (:347), the test model is left running; the put-back restart then finds no room (17-changes.mjs:583) and the owner's model stays down. The put-back also runs without a validation mark, so if restart_model itself is the version that failed its check it is refused (16-actions.mjs:341-356), as the earlier audit found and the code still shows.
kept.failure: Spark 3 runs model A with room to spare; the test model fits beside it. The run passes, yet the log (and the installer output through tools/console.mjs) says 'Couldn’t start A again: A is running.' Second case: the test model's stop fails; the test ends with the test model up and A down, with only a 'Couldn’t start' line.
kept.ownerSays: Test the changes and tell me exactly what you stopped and what is back.
kept.build: If decision 4 stands, cut test_changes and validateChanged; fix nothing. If it stays: in the finally block stop the test container first (ignore 'not running'), and treat outcome 'already' as 'Left X running'. Two lines, one test.
guards: Never touches Spark 2 or a model across two Sparks
Put-back never stops anything the test did not start
kept.ownerDecision: The 2026-11-11 delegated decision 4 drops the 'validated on these Sparks' step. If that is still the plan, cut test_changes instead of fixing it.

kept.title: The full gate cannot pass on Spark 2: tests read the real releases folder
kept.gap: The stand-in console keeps the real HOME. test/start-mock.mjs:147-158 passes process.env through and sets the state folder, socket and secrets file, but not the releases folder. service/src/18-workflows.mjs:363 then falls back to ~/.local/share/spark-console/releases. On the Mac that folder does not exist. On Spark 2 it holds up to 10 real snapshots (deploy/host-on-portal.sh:109, :163). test/validate.test.mjs:133-136 asserts `{available:false, stamp:null}` and a 404. Only internet.test.mjs:25 and telegram.test.mjs:28 set SPARK_CONSOLE_RELEASES. So test/lock.mjs never writes a lock on Spark 2, and the installer refuses (host-on-portal.sh:57). The comment at start-mock.mjs:3 says HOME is stood in; that is true for the fake Sparks only.
kept.failure: On Spark 2, after any install: node test/lock.mjs. validate.test.mjs 'going back to the last good build: none on the stand-in fleet' gets available:true and a 202. The suite fails, no lock is written, and no self-built change can ever be installed.
kept.ownerSays: Run the full tests on Spark 2 and tell me if they pass.
kept.build: One line in test/start-mock.mjs: default SPARK_CONSOLE_RELEASES to an empty folder inside the run's temp dir (extraEnv still overrides). Test that fails without it: start the stand-in with HOME pointing at a temp folder that holds .local/share/spark-console/releases/<stamp>/restore.sh and assert GET /rollback says available:false. Then run the whole gate once on Spark 2 before handoff; that is the only proof nothing else leaks from the real home.
guards: Harness change only; no existing assertion is edited or weakened
The stand-in still never calls systemd-run (18-workflows.mjs:383)

kept.title: An update leaves no record that outlives its own restart: not the ask, the yes, the install or the undo
kept.gap: Installing restarts the console that is driving the install. Everything about the update lives in memory or in a folder name. Open buttons are an in-memory Map kept 15 minutes (service/src/17-changes.mjs:41, :52-53); the gate takes about an hour, so an owner's yes asked through it would expire first. docs/architecture.md:258 lists jobs, claims and open buttons as lost at restart. A snapshot is named by time only and holds no build id (deploy/host-on-portal.sh:109-126). A new build announces itself only in the journal (service/src/25-backup-and-start.mjs:63). undo_update writes one audit line with the stamp it went to, not the build it left (18-workflows.mjs:393), in a file that rotates at 10 MB (20-mcp.mjs:131). restore.sh puts back the installed files only (host-on-portal.sh:138-146), so ~/spark-console-src still holds the undone code with a lock that matches it (:57) and the next `local` install brings the bad build back. sparkie_setup reports build and lockIsForThisBuild (16-actions.mjs:788) but not whether the source copy is the running build, so Sparkie can read docs and code for a build that is not running.
kept.failure: Sparkie installs build B; the restart ends its turn. Nothing tells the owner B is running or checks it live. B misbehaves; the owner says undo. Next day Sparkie is asked for a small fix, edits nothing relevant, and installs from the unchanged source: B is back, with no note it was undone.
kept.ownerSays: What changed in Spark Console this week, and did anything get undone?
kept.build: One state file, newest 20 lines: {at, build, previousBuild, stamp, result}. install.sh appends a line; undoUpdate appends {undid: BUILD}. At start, if BUILD differs from the last build announced, one notice ('Spark Console is now build X, was Y') on events and Telegram. sparkie_setup returns the last five. No refusal rule, no lesson field, no live-check field.
guards: State is untouched by restore.sh without --with-state, so the record survives a rollback
Holds no secret; added to architecture.md section 4
The owner's yes is re-checked against the lock's build at install time, never trusted from the file alone
kept.ownerDecision: Should a build you undid be refused for re-install until its source changes? Recommended: yes, with a force word only you can give.

kept.title: A snapshot cut short by a full disk hides every good one from undo and is never cleaned up
kept.gap: install.sh makes the snapshot folder first and writes restore.sh last (deploy/host-on-portal.sh:121-127, :160). If the disk fills while state is copied, set -e stops the install and leaves a folder with no restore.sh. The prune of old snapshots runs only after a good snapshot (:163), so each retry adds another partial folder to a disk that is already full. lastSnapshot looks at the newest folder only and gives up if it has no restore.sh (service/src/18-workflows.mjs:366-368). restore.sh itself deletes the live files, then copies (:138), so a full disk or a reboot mid-restore leaves an empty install that the watchdog can only restart, not repair (:250-262). The earlier plan said restore.sh 'swaps by rename' (docs/analysis-2026-11-11/01-gap-analysis-plan.md:46); as built it does not. The earlier fix for undo (skip a snapshot of the same build) does not cover a folder with no restore.sh.
kept.failure: Disk on Spark 2 is nearly full. An update is tried twice; both stop while saving state. The running build has a fault. 'Undo the last update' answers 'There's no earlier build to go back to', though nine complete snapshots are on disk.
kept.ownerSays: If the disk fills up during an update, can you still go back?
kept.build: lastSnapshot walks newest to oldest and returns the first folder that has restore.sh (two lines, one test in validate.test.mjs). install.sh removes its own half-made snapshot folder when the save fails. Nothing else.
guards: The live folders stay the same folders, so Tailscale's routes and the short-address mount keep working (host-on-portal.sh:136-137)
Never deletes a complete snapshot beyond the newest-10 rule

kept.title: docs/architecture.md states a build, a part count and line numbers that are already wrong, and nothing checks it
kept.gap: Sparkie is told to read this map second (AGENTS.md:8-14) and to trust it over the contract (architecture.md:265). Its header says 'Checked against the code on 2026-11-11, build f9e9701cec75 (32 parts' (architecture.md:3); service/src holds 33 parts and the lock is for build aca03d1af018 (service/workflows.lock.json). Section 8 says 'The tree is not locked now. The lock names build 4f371d567af6' (:254), which is no longer true. It cites startModel at 17-changes.mjs:404, railsFor :96, placeModel :133, bestHow :164, runAction 16-actions.mjs:286, sparkieCheck :251 (:114-115); they are at :411, :103, :140, :171, :294, :259. Section 7 item 3 hard-codes 'the 24 and 37 counts' (:240). code-map.md has a test (test/build.test.mjs:16-17); this file has none. Another agent is editing parts now, so some drift is minutes old; that is the point: every edit makes it staler and nothing says so.
kept.failure: Sparkie, on a smaller brain, opens 17-changes.mjs at line 404 as the map says, lands in a different function, and patches the wrong place; or reads 'the tree is not locked' and runs an hour-long gate it did not need.
kept.ownerSays: Is the architecture map still true for the build that's running?
kept.build: Delete the volatile facts only: the build id and part count in the header, the 'not locked now' trap, and the literal 24 and 37 in checklist item 3 (with BI-4). Say once that the live build and lock come from sparkie_setup. Extend tools/code-map.mjs --check with one rule: every NN-name.mjs named in architecture.md exists. Leave line numbers alone.
guards: Rules R1-R33 and their wording are not changed, only how they point at code
Checklist item 13 (the map changes in the same change) stays

kept.title: After a brain swap nothing knows whether the new brain passed the eval, and the eval record does not name a brain
kept.gap: The contract makes the eval part of every self-change that touches instructions or a workflow (docs/contract.md:396-397). test/eval.mjs writes results to a dated file in the source tree with time, cases and scores, but not which model answered or which console build was under test (test/eval.mjs:130-134). The only result on disk is a partial run from 2026-11-08 (test/eval/results-2026-11-08-partial.json). Its header tells the reader to tunnel from 'this computer' (:10-15), though --brain-port works on Spark 2 itself. The lock and sparkie_setup say nothing about the eval (service/src/16-actions.mjs:788). The owner swaps the brain; from then on every self-change is designed and judged by a model nobody measured on this tool list.
kept.failure: Owner swaps Qwen for a newer build of it. Sparkie keeps accepting 'change the console' requests. The last eval on record is for the old brain and an older tool list, and nothing shows that.

kept.title: A build that crashes after the first 45 seconds is never put back, and nobody is told
kept.gap: The installer counts an update as good after one /health answer naming the build (deploy/host-on-portal.sh:207-213). After that only the watchdog looks, and it can only restart: it acts on state 'failed' or on 'active' with 3 missed /health (host-on-portal.sh:239-256). The unit is Restart=always, RestartSec=3 (:187-193), so a crash loop sits in 'activating' and never reaches 'failed'; the case statement matches nothing. A crash from a timer (uncaughtException exits, 25-backup-and-start.mjs:89-92; adoptRunning runs 60 s after start, architecture.md:104) gives a console that restarts every minute while /health answers in between, so misses reset. The watchdog never runs restore.sh, and the service never reads watchdog-restarts (no match for 'watchdog' in service/src), so the owner is never told. The earlier review asked for a watchdog that puts the last good build back (reviews-2026-11-11.md:104-107); the built one lacks that piece. Installer, restore.sh and watchdog run under no test (architecture.md:263).
kept.failure: Install a build whose 60-second timer throws. The installer says health ok. The console then restarts about once a minute for ever, cutting every chat and Telegram turn. Nothing rolls back; the owner must SSH in and run restore.sh.
kept.ownerSays: Did the last update stick, or did you go back?
kept.build: BI-1's settle window covers the first minute after an install. For later loops add one thing: the watchdog reads NRestarts, and when it grew by 3 or more in 10 minutes writes a small note file; the console reads it at start and sends one notice plus Telegram. Telling the owner is the missing piece; the automatic restore stays with the earlier plan.
guards: At most one automatic go-back per snapshot; never touches SSH, Tailscale, firewall, users or any model
Goes back only to a build the owner already approved (the one before the update)
A console stopped on purpose is still left alone

The lock check compares only the build id of server.mjs, dig.mjs and passkey.mjs (:48, :54-57), so a worker.py-only edit installs with every workflow off and crash restarts off (architecture.md R29, :207). The four checks planned for update_console (01-gap-analysis-plan.md:75) live in an action that does not exist, so no install path has them today.

guards: Checks read only; the one action called is a read

kept.title: An install cannot be started from inside the console without killing itself
kept.gap: `host-on-portal.sh local` exists (:29-33) but only works from a terminal. Three traps for a console-started install: (a) `systemctl --user restart spark-console-api` (:198) kills every child of the service, the installer included, before the health check, the restore and the source swap; undoUpdate already avoids this with systemd-run (18-workflows.mjs:383-392) but nothing does it for install. (b) The busy check counts chats answering (:115-128, :300-311); an install asked for in chat always sees its own turn as busy, then reads /dev/tty for a yes, which does not exist, and stops with "Nothing was changed". (c) In local mode the result is printed to a terminal nobody reads; nothing is posted back to the chat after the restart (tgAfterRestart only says a turn was cut, 21-telegram.mjs:311-319). The planned update_console (reviews:101, 01-plan:75) does not name these.
kept.failure: Owner says "install it" in chat. Whatever runs the script from the service dies at the restart with files half checked, or refuses as busy. The owner hears nothing and must open a terminal.
kept.ownerSays: The tests passed, go ahead and install it.
kept.build: One owner-only path, shaped like undoUpdate: after the owner's yes, write state file pending-install.json {conv, by, sourceBuild, askedAt}, then `systemd-run --user --collect --on-active=3 --unit spark-console-install bash ~/spark-console-src/deploy/host-on-portal.sh local` with ASSUME_YES=1 only when the sole busy item is the asking chat. The installer appends its outcome (installed, went back, refused, with the last lines) to the same file. At start the console reads it, posts the outcome in that chat and on Telegram, and removes it. Refuse if a unit of that name is active. Test (stand-in systemd-run that records its arguments): fails unless the unit is started outside the service, a second request is refused, and a restart with a pending file posts the result in the chat.
guards: Owner on the tailnet or a passkey press only, same rule as undo_update (18-workflows.mjs:412-420); never an agent key, a workflow step or Telegram alone

kept.title: A full disk or a cut-off install leaves a half-installed console, and a failed restore leaves it stopped for good
kept.gap: The installer only puts the old build back when the new one fails to answer /health in 45 s (deploy/host-on-portal.sh:216-232). Every step before that runs under `set -euo pipefail` (:66) with no trap. The UI is copied file by file (:174), the short-address copy is deleted then copied (:177), and the service files are copied straight over the live ones (:180). If any copy fails (disk full, session cut, console restarting the installer's own process group at :197 when run from inside the console), the script just exits. The running process still has the old code in memory, so /health looks fine, but the next restart (watchdog, crash, reboot) loads a mixed or truncated server.mjs. restore.sh has the same shape: it stops the service (:140), then put_back deletes the live folder before copying (:138). If that copy fails the service folder is empty and the service is stopped, and the watchdog only acts on `failed` or `active` (:258-259), never on stopped. The snapshot also copies the whole state folder each time and keeps 10 (:124, :162-163), with no free-space check, so installs themselves push toward the full disk. 01-gap-analysis-plan.md:46 already asked for restore.sh to swap by rename; it is not built, and the install side was never raised.
kept.failure: Spark 2's disk fills during `cp "$IN"/service/*` (line 180). The installer exits 1 with server.mjs half-written. The console keeps running the old code from memory. Hours later the watchdog or a reboot restarts it; node fails to parse server.mjs; systemd loops; the watchdog restarts 3 times then stops trying. Sparkie is down and cannot fix itself; the owner needs SSH.
kept.ownerSays: "Update yourself" and, if the disk is full, hear "Not installed: Spark 2 has 2 GB free and the update needs 6. Nothing changed."
kept.build: Three small edits, no rename: (1) a free-space check before the snapshot, in plain words; (2) after the snapshot, `trap 'bash "$SNAP/restore.sh"' ERR` until the health check passes; (3) restore.sh gets `trap 'systemctl --user start spark-console-api' EXIT` so it never leaves the unit stopped. Prove it with the stub-systemctl installer test (self-fix/gate-2): a cp that fails mid-install leaves the service folder as before and the service started.
guards: Never touches the systemd unit's Tailscale routes, SSH or sudo paths

kept.title: The gate leaves nothing behind but the lock: a failed or interrupted hour is lost, and Sparkie has nothing to read to fix the failure
kept.gap: test/lock.mjs runs the suite with stdio inherited (:25) and writes a file only on full success (:38-39). A failure prints one line (:27) and exits. There is no record of which tests failed, how long each file took, on which machine and Node version, or that a run was started at all. If the terminal closes, Spark 2 reboots or the console restarts mid-run, the hour is gone without trace. The lock is written with plain writeFileSync (:39), not write-then-rename, so a cut at that moment leaves a truncated lock, which the service reads as "no lock" and switches every workflow off (18-workflows.mjs:74, :81). Flaky tests are known (07-fast-gate-plan.md section 3) but flake history lives in the builder's memory ("gate8", "gate22"). Running the gate from inside the console would also put it under the unit's MemoryMax=512M (deploy/host-on-portal.sh:195). The earlier plans propose update_console and a container gate (reviews-2026-11-11.md:99-101; 01-gap-analysis-plan.md:74-75) and dropped the test harness as a chat job (10-round-two-report.md:99); none of them says where the result lives. The blockers in 07 section 5 are also still open (05-library.mjs:52 reads /proc/meminfo first; 18-workflows.mjs:363 reads the real releases folder unless a test sets it; 02-ssh.mjs:7 sleeps 1 s).
kept.failure: Sparkie starts the gate on Spark 2 for a change. Forty minutes in, state.test fails on a timing race. The run ends with "The suite didn't pass". Sparkie's turn has ended; nothing on disk names the failing test. The next attempt starts from zero, and Sparkie cannot tell a real failure from the known flake.
kept.ownerSays: "Run the tests", walk away, and later ask "did they pass?" from Telegram: "No. 657 of 659 passed; the two that failed are in state.test, and both have failed on timing twice this week."
kept.build: lock.mjs runs each test file itself (07-fast-gate-plan cut 2, which also removes the glob problem in works/gate-1): one child per file, output to test/.gate/<file>.log, and one test/.gate/last.json {startedAt, endedAt, host, node, build, ok, files:[{file, ok, seconds}]} written at start with ok:null and rewritten at the end. Sparkie reads the failing file's log. Write the lock by temp file and rename. One read-only `gate` line in fleet_status.console from last.json.
guards: The quick check never writes the lock (07 section 4 stands)
The gate never touches the real Sparks or the live console's state folder: fix 07 section 5 items 1-2 before any run on Spark 2
Nothing here starts a model on Spark 2; the stand-in fleet is bash scripts

kept.title: Going back a build forgets that the old build was already proven on the real Sparks
kept.gap: validations.json keeps one validated version per workflow (18-workflows.mjs:82: `v.version === version`), and a passing run of a new version overwrites it (:90-91). Undo restores files, not state (deploy/host-on-portal.sh:129-131, :226; architecture.md "restores files, not state"). So after update then undo, every workflow whose code differed between the two builds reads "needs-validation" on the old build, although that exact version ran on these Sparks for days. The owner's own request still runs as its validation (16-actions.mjs:346), but an agent's call is refused (:357), a start that only fits across two Sparks is refused for anyone but the owner's direct words (17-changes.mjs:406-407), and the page asks for a confirm (18-workflows.mjs:105-108). The safe path (rollback) is the one that drops trust. The same happens in the other direction on a re-install of a build that was validated before.

kept.title: The daily copy forgets its last good run at every restart, can replace today's good copy with a cut-off one, and waits a day when Spark 3 and 4 are off
kept.gap: lastBackup is a variable (25-backup-and-start.mjs:5). After any restart /health shows null for ten minutes (:34; 24-handler.mjs:56), and a failed try overwrites the last good one (:9, :25), so "when was the last good copy" is never known. The file is named by day (:10). The remote side moves the .part into place as soon as the stream ends (:13), before the local side has judged tar's exit code (:25); if tar fails or the 180 s timer kills it (:19), the stream still closes cleanly and a truncated archive replaces that day's good copy, and it counts toward the 14 kept. The target is Spark 3, else any Spark not known offline (:8); Spark 3 and 4 are powered down by the owner as a matter of course, and then the only message is "tries again tomorrow" (:26) while the timer simply waits 24 h (:34). Retry-when-a-Spark-returns and a stale-backup line are already proposed (reviews-2026-11-11.md:110; 01-gap-analysis-plan.md:58); the lost last-good time and the overwrite are not.

kept.title: Spark cannot gate or install by itself: the as-built `local` mode breaks four ways when the console starts it
kept.gap: No action runs the gate or the installer (action list in service/src: only test_changes and undo_update, 18-workflows.mjs:397-422). The planned update_console (01-gap-analysis-plan.md:73-78) is unbuilt, and the plan misses these as-built facts. (1) The console unit has MemoryMax=512M and Restart=always (deploy/host-on-portal.sh:192-195); a gate or installer started as a child lives in that cgroup, so the gate (about 430 processes per scan) can get the console killed. (2) install.sh runs `systemctl --user restart spark-console-api` (:202); as a child it is killed with the service, so the health check and put-back (:215-231) never run. Same root as install-3, still open at :334. (3) The busy check (:320-329) reads /dev/tty; Sparkie asking for the install is itself `replying >= 1`, so with no terminal it always ends 'Nothing was changed'. (4) The routes step runs `tailscale serve status` under set -e and falls back to `sudo tailscale serve` (:338-344), which rule R3 forbids unattended. Also every install rewrites the unit and the watchdog (:184-283) and swaps ~/spark-console-src for the tar, deleting anything outside the tar list such as .git (:234-240, :51-52).
kept.failure: Owner says 'install the fix'. Sparkie has no tool; if it ran `bash deploy/host-on-portal.sh local` through any runner it would stop at the busy prompt, or be killed at the restart with no put-back.
kept.ownerSays: Test your own code. / Install it.
kept.build: One action update_console {step:'test'|'install'}, owner only with undo's existing ownerHere rule. Each step starts with systemd-run --user --collect as undoUpdate does (18-workflows.mjs:463): test = `nice node test/lock.mjs` in its own unit with its own memory cap; install = `bash ~/spark-console-src/deploy/host-on-portal.sh local`. Two installer edits: with no terminal, wait until idle instead of asking; in local mode skip the routes step entirely. Move the heredoc to deploy/install.sh only when the installer test (self-fix/gate-2) needs it. Container gate and `self` mode later.
guards: Owner only, on the tailnet or with the passkey; never an agent key, a workflow step or Telegram without the page button

Gate unit is capped and niced so the brain on Spark 2 is not starved; it starts no model

kept.title: Nothing carries an outcome across a restart, so the owner hears nothing after an install, a put-back, an undo, a crash loop or a watchdog restart
kept.gap: The console posts no event at start: event types are notice, operation, healing, heal-skipped, started, removed, learned; none says 'console started on build X'. tgAfterRestart only speaks if a turn was cut (21-telegram.mjs:311-320). An uncaught error is printed and the process exits (25-backup-and-start.mjs:89-92); with Restart=always and RestartSec=3 systemd restarts it for ever, and the watchdog zeroes its miss count whenever /health answers (host-on-portal.sh:260), so a build that dies every few minutes is never noticed or undone. The watchdog logs with `logger` (:252-254) and the rollback unit's output is dropped (18-workflows.mjs:385, stdio ignore, --collect); service_logs reads only the console unit's last 100 lines (service/worker.py:219-222), so Sparkie cannot see either. undoUpdate says 'Going back' before anything ran (18-workflows.mjs:394-395).
kept.failure: A new build passes the 45-second check, then throws on its first backup at 10 minutes (25-backup-and-start.mjs:34). It restarts every 10 minutes, cutting chats and jobs. No notice, no rollback, no count anywhere the owner or Sparkie reads.

At start one function reads both and posts one notice: updated to X; the update did not start, back on W; went back to W; or restarted N times in 10 minutes on X with the last error and the existing owner-only 'go back a build' button. Never rolls back unasked. Same lines in fleet_status.console.

kept.title: The brain's saved choice is never checked against the brain container that is running
kept.gap: Which setup is the brain is one field, `current` in main.json, read once at start (service/src/13-main-model.mjs:12-17). Nothing compares it with the `sparkie-main` container, whose labels carry only the served name (13-main-model.mjs:129). Four ways they drift apart: (a) switchMain stops the old brain, starts the new one in the same container name, and saves the choice only after it answers (13-main-model.mjs:251-264), so a console restart, watchdog restart or crash during the up-to-45-minute load leaves the new model running and the console believing the old one; (b) an unreadable main.json is moved aside by readKept (13-main-model.mjs:10) and `current` silently becomes the first preset in config.json (13-main-model.mjs:14), dropping any owner-made `lib-…` preset and the chat/agent routes (13-main-model.mjs:36); (c) `restore.sh --with-state` copies an older main.json back (deploy/host-on-portal.sh:147-148); (d) an install or rollback replaces config.json, so a preset id can vanish or its args change while the container keeps the old ones. In every case mainStatus says healthy (the port answers), watchBrain does nothing (service/src/20-heal.mjs:145), chat sends `model: MAIN.served` (13-main-model.mjs:45), and `/main/use` refuses to switch back with 'already Sparkie's model' (service/src/24-handler.mjs:579). All four shipped presets share served name qwen-aphex on SGLang (service/config.json:33), which hides this today; the first owner swap to a newer model (the one path the fixed rules reserve for the owner) removes that cover. writeMainFile also uses a fixed `.tmp` name and its own writer instead of writePrivate (13-main-model.mjs:27-30).
kept.failure: Owner swaps the brain to a library model served by vLLM; Spark Console is restarted by the watchdog while it loads. After the restart main.json still names the old preset, the container serves the new model under another name, every chat call gets 404 for the model name, self-healing sees a healthy brain, and the page refuses to pick the old preset because it is 'already' current. Same result if main.json is damaged after a finished swap: the owner's swap is forgotten and the next brain start would bring back the old Qwen.
kept.ownerSays: "Which model is your brain right now, and does it match what I picked?"
kept.build: Add --label spark.setup=<id> in mainRunCommand; print it in mainStatusScript; once at start, if the running label names a known preset other than MAIN.id, adopt it and write one notice; if it names nothing known, or 'current' names a missing preset, keep MAIN and write the notice. writeMainFile calls writePrivate. No 'switching' record.
guards: Reconcile only reads Docker and writes main.json; it never starts, stops or restarts the brain.
Adopt only a preset id that exists in config.json or main.json; never build a setup from container args.
Only the owner's /main/use changes which model runs; this only makes the console say what is true.

kept.title: A damaged state file is set aside and nothing brings it back
kept.gap: readKept moves a file that is not JSON to `<file>.unreadable-<time>` and returns empty, with a notice that says 'nothing was lost' (service/src/03-identity.mjs:10-25). For serving that means: verified.json empty -> bestHow has no proven runs and every start falls back to a recipe or the engine's defaults (service/src/09-verified.mjs:6, 17-changes.mjs:164); added-models.json empty -> the owner's added models leave Recipes (10-recipes.mjs:5-8); found-setups.json empty -> rebuilt at 20 models a day (11-setups.mjs:217, :231-241); desired.json gone -> watchHeld sees no file and seeds a new list from whatever runs at that minute (20-desired.mjs:64-70), so models that were held or on a powered-off Spark 3/4 are forgotten and never healed. No tool lets Sparkie put a set-aside file back; the only copies are the daily tar on another Spark (skipped when that Spark is off) and install snapshots. writePrivate renames without syncing the temp file (03-identity.mjs:27-32), so a Spark 2 power loss can leave exactly this, and a failed write (full disk) leaves `<file>.<pid>.tmp` behind for good.
kept.failure: Spark 2 loses power while a start finishes. verified.json comes back empty or cut short. Next 'start GLM' picks the engine defaults instead of the proven two-Spark run, fails or runs slow, and Sparkie reports it as a normal start. If desired.json was the damaged file and Spark 3 is off, the list is reseeded empty and nothing comes back when Spark 3 powers on.
kept.ownerSays: "Did any of your saved files get damaged, and did you get them back?"
kept.build: 03-identity.mjs, two functions. writePrivate: before the rename, copy the current good file to `<file>.prev` (copyFileSync), fsync the temp file, and unlink the temp file if the write throws. readKept: when the file is not JSON, set it aside as today, then read `<file>.prev`; if that parses, write it back as the file and change the notice to 'restored from the last good copy (one save may be missing)'. 20-desired.mjs:64: seed only when neither desired.json nor any desired.json.unreadable-* exists. Test in test/state.test.mjs beside :181: write a good verified.json through the service, then garbage over it -> verified runs are still listed and the notice says restored; fails today (list is empty).
guards: Never write over a file that exists but cannot be read (R20 stays).
.prev files hold no secrets beyond what the file already holds; keep them 0600 in the state folder.
One writer per file stays as is (R22).

kept.title: A new engine image in config.json installs as tested and validated without either
kept.gap: The build id covers server.mjs, dig.mjs and passkey.mjs only (service/src/01-setup.mjs:17-21; deploy/host-on-portal.sh:48, :56-57). A workflow's version covers its functions, ENGINES, the action and worker.py (service/src/18-workflows.mjs:59-69), not CONFIG.images, CONFIG.imageSources or the brain presets, which all live in service/config.json (config.json:26-33) and are replaced on every install and put back on every rollback. So changing the default vLLM or SGLang digest, or the trusted image sources, changes no build id and no workflow version: the lock still matches, `start_model` stays 'validated on your Sparks', and agents may run it at once on an engine that has never started here. After handoff this is exactly the edit Sparkie will make to move to a newer engine. Separately, catalog.json is parsed with no guard on every call (01-setup.mjs:24; 10-recipes.mjs:10) and I found no parse check for it in the installer, so a cut-short catalog.json makes every start_model, find_recipes and bestHow throw a JSON error while /health stays ok.
kept.failure: Sparkie edits config.json to a newer vLLM digest, the owner approves, the install passes (same build, same lock). The first agent-run start_model uses the new image as a validated workflow; if the image is broken on GB10, a bystander model was already stopped to make room.
kept.ownerSays: "Move vLLM to the newer image and tell me when it has been proven on a Spark."
kept.build: Hash CONFIG.images and CONFIG.imageSources only (never servePort) into the start and restart workflow versions. In host-on-portal.sh, parse config.json and catalog.json with python3 before staging and refuse on error. Skip the 503 wrapper.
guards: Do not put config.json into the build id: that would force the one-hour gate for a brain preset edit and switch every workflow off.
The owner's validation run stays the only way a new image becomes usable by agents.
kept.ownerDecision: Should a change to the brain's own presets in config.json also need a named owner step (a brain restart check), or stay as today?

kept.title: What is in use and what was stopped on purpose is forgotten at every restart
kept.gap: Three facts that guard starts live only in memory: `inUse` (a model answered calls in the last 30 minutes; service/src/15-routes.mjs:76-78, written at :167), `consoleStopped` (stopped on purpose; 18-workflows.mjs:244) and `callStarts` (15-routes.mjs:106). start_model asks before stopping a model only if `usedRecently` says so (17-changes.mjs:443, :492), and a call to /v1 refuses to restart a model 'stopped on purpose N min ago' only from `consoleStopped` (15-routes.mjs:119-120). Every console update, rollback, watchdog restart or crash empties all three (architecture.md section 4 lists them as not kept). After handoff, updates are routine, and Sparkie carries on working straight after one.
kept.failure: An app is calling GLM on Spark 3. The owner approves a console update; it restarts. Two minutes later Sparkie runs 'start the coder model': placement picks Spark 3, `usedRecently` is empty, GLM is stopped without the 'it is in use' question. Second case: owner says 'stop GLM', console restarts, the app's next retry starts GLM again on a call because the purposeful stop is no longer known.
kept.ownerSays: "You just updated yourself. Is anything in use that I should not stop?"
kept.build: No new file. usedRecently treats any running console model as in use while the service has been up under 30 minutes (by: 'unknown, Spark Console restarted'). startOnCall also refuses when a desired.json revision in the last 30 minutes removed that container. Two small edits and one test.
guards: It only adds a question before a stop; it never blocks the owner's explicit yes.
No request text or caller key in the file: container, time and a display name only.

kept.title: A full disk is an unknown failure on Spark 3/4 and a silent loss on Spark 2
kept.gap: START_FAILURES has no entry for 'no space left on device' (service/src/17-changes.mjs:201-245; the image entry at :231 does not match it), so a full disk during an image pull, a model copy (07-jobs.mjs:99-112), a download or an engine cache write reads as an unknown failure with a raw log, after other models may already have been stopped. On Spark 2, a failed state write after a good start is swallowed: desiredAfter only logs to the service log (20-desired.mjs:38), so the model that just started is not on the should-run list and will never be healed, and recordVerified only adds a job note (09-verified.mjs:113), so the proven run is lost. Nothing tells the owner. Console-made leftovers that fill disks are also invisible to the library scan, which skips hidden folders: `~/models/.incoming` and `hub/.spark-console-incoming` from a copy cut off by a console restart (07-jobs.mjs:89, :107 cleans only inside the live process), one engine cache folder per image ever used (05-library.mjs:350-353), and `<name>-before-<job>` containers (08-cluster.mjs:353). The planned free_disk workflow (reviews-2026-11-11.md, 'Downloads and disk') has no list of these to work from.
kept.failure: Spark 2's disk fills. Owner starts GLM on Spark 3; it loads and answers; Sparkie says done. desired.json was not written. Spark 3 is powered off and on next day: GLM does not come back and should_be_running does not list it.
kept.ownerSays: "Is any disk close to full, and what of yours can go?"
kept.build: Only this: when writePrivate fails in desiredAfter or recordVerified, raise one fleetEvent notice naming the file and the model ('X is running but not on the should-run list'). Disk-full row via serving-heal-7; leftovers with free_disk.
guards: Nothing is deleted here: leftovers are only listed. Removing them stays with the planned free_disk workflow and the owner's yes.
Never count the owner's models or the Hugging Face cache as leftovers.

kept.title: A proven run records the tag that was asked for, not the build and weights that ran
kept.gap: A verified run's key and record hold the image string as given and no weights revision (service/src/09-verified.mjs:95, :108-111). The image can be a plain version tag: the brain presets use `lmsysorg/sglang:v0.5.23` with the real build only in `imageId` on Spark 2 (service/config.json:33-), and dig accepts pinned tags without a digest (service/dig.mjs:323). plainFromBrain and resolveHow then reuse `v.image` on another Spark (11-setups.mjs:278, :309), where Docker pulls whatever the tag points at now. Weights are the same: every start resolves `refs/main` or the newest snapshot (01-setup.mjs hfSnap), so after a re-download the 'worked here before' run and its measured speed describe a different revision. The entry never says which build or revision it was measured on, and `best` never ages, so recipe_detail and bestHow present it as current.
kept.failure: The brain's proven setup is reused to start the same Qwen on Spark 3. Spark 3 has no local copy of the tag, pulls today's build of it, and the start fails or answers garbage, although the plan said 'the brain's proven setup'.
kept.ownerSays: "That run you call proven: which engine build and which weights was it on?"
kept.build: In recordVerified, when the image is not a digest, read the container image's RepoDigest once and store it on the entry; plainFromBrain runs image@digest when it is there. Or simply pin the brain presets by digest at the owner's next brain change. Skip snapshot tracking.
guards: Read-only inspect; no image is pulled to learn a digest.
Digest still has to be from a trusted image source (resolveHow's check stays).

kept.title: 'Look it up now' can return a 12-hour-old read stamped as fresh
kept.gap: find_setups promises setups 'looked up now' (service/src/17-changes.mjs:630-633). digModel reads the sources through cachedIndex, six hours in memory (11-setups.mjs:50-56), on top of webGet's own six-hour cache (11-setups.mjs:8), and pins image tags through pinCache, six hours (11-setups.mjs:94-98). The result is stamped `at: now` (11-setups.mjs:197-198), which also resets the weekly freshness clock (11-setups.mjs:217). So a look the owner asks for after NVIDIA publishes a recipe can return the old list, say it is fresh, and stop the daily refresher from trying again for a week. A console restart clears the caches, so the same question gives a different answer after an update, with nothing to tell the two apart.
kept.failure: Owner: 'NVIDIA just posted a recipe for GLM, find its setups.' The daily look ran four hours ago. find_setups finishes in seconds with the old setups, recipe_detail shows them as looked up just now, and the new recipe is not seen for seven days.
kept.ownerSays: "Check again for GLM setups, and tell me when you last really read each source."
kept.build: In the find_setups action only (service/src/17-changes.mjs:651-665), clear indexes, webCache and pinCache before startDig. The daily look keeps its caches. One test that drives cachedIndex.
guards: The daily look keeps its caches and its 20-a-day cap, so GitHub's anonymous rate limit is not hit.
Commands are still read by code and vetted by dig.vetSetup; nothing new reaches the brain.

kept.title: A stopped, missing or crash-looping brain stays down, and nothing says so
kept.gap: The fixed rule is that Qwen on Spark 2 is always running, but the code only heals a brain that is running and silent. service/src/20-heal.mjs:145 resets the timer whenever state is not 'running', so exited, missing and Docker's 'restarting' loop are all ignored. The restart count is read (service/src/13-main-model.mjs:87-90) and used nowhere. A failed switch can leave no container at all: switchMain stops the old one (13-main-model.mjs:251), startMain removes it (:202), and if the old setup fails too it only writes a job note (:258). The owner's words then point at a page screen: '/restart sparkie' answers 'Start it from Models' (service/src/20-words.mjs:52), /status says only 'stopped' (:22), chat says 'Start it from Models' (service/src/14-chats.mjs:305). The only start is the page route POST /main/start (service/src/24-handler.mjs:586-593). The 01 gap plan lists a 'brain keeper' in phase 1; it is not in the code, and it did not cover the crash loop or the words.
kept.failure: A brain switch fails and the old setup does not come back either (or the container is removed, or it crash-loops on a bad kernel cache). Result: no event, no heal, Sparkie cannot answer, Telegram says 'Spark Console restarts it by itself' (service/src/21-telegram.mjs:18), which is untrue. A human must call POST /main/start or use a terminal.
kept.ownerSays: "/restart sparkie" when it is down, and it starts. Or nothing: "Sparkie's model was missing, so I started it again at 14:02."
kept.build: Two rules, no record lookup. (1) Container missing (never 'exited') and no brain job running: watchBrain starts the same setup through the existing main-start job with every GPU user in keep, at most twice in 6 hours, with one 'healing' event. (2) '/restart sparkie' on an exited or missing brain starts it the same way; /status says 'stopped' or 'missing, starting it'. Exited stays down: that is a stop by hand or by the console. One notice for a 'restarting' loop; fix the Telegram line that says it restarts by itself.
guards: Same setup only; never a different model or preset (no fallback brain).
Never stops anything on Spark 2 to make room; a brain the owner stopped stays down.
At most twice in 6 hours, never while a main-start, main-stop or main-switch job runs.
startMain is not in any workflow's code list, so no workflow needs validating again.
kept.ownerDecision: A brain you stopped by hand stays down until you say so (recommended yes, as the 01 plan's skeptics ruled).

kept.title: A one-Spark model comes back by itself only after an exit-255 power loss
kept.gap: For a one-Spark entry on the should-run list, healPass has one path: its Spark came back AND every part exited 255 (service/src/20-heal.mjs:68-69), else 'return null' (:77). Your own clean power-off is 'systemctl poweroff' (deploy/power-setup.sh:13-14), where Docker stops containers first, so the exit code is likely 0, 137 or 143, not 255 (not checked on a Spark). The 04 audit's fix said 'exited 255 or finished before the on time'; only the first half was built. The crash path (maybeHeal) runs once, on the watcher's transition (service/src/19-watcher.mjs:104); a skip for a passing reason, such as 'Spark was offline in the last half hour' (service/src/18-workflows.mjs:263-264, any Wi-Fi blip on Spark 4), is never tried again. If the container is gone, bring-back calls restart_model, which answers 404 (service/src/17-changes.mjs:567-568; 20-heal.mjs:109; 24-handler.mjs:520), so even the owner's 'bring it back' fails. The contract promises the opposite for 'the owner's power cycles' (docs/contract.md:1275-1282).
kept.failure: You power Spark 3 off cleanly with gemma running, then on again. Result: gemma stays stopped, held as 'it isn't running' (service/src/20-desired.mjs:54), until you ask. A two-Spark model in the same case does come back (20-heal.mjs:78-81), so the two behave differently. Or: docker prune removed the container; 'bring it back' fails with 'isn't one of Spark Console's models'.
kept.ownerSays: Nothing after a power-on: "Spark 3 came back on, so I started gemma again." Or "bring gemma back" works even when its container was removed.
kept.build: Now: in bringBack and POST /desired/bring-back, when the container is gone call start_model {model, spark} with noStops. Then read the real exit code after one clean power-off (workloads shows it, no SSH). Only if it is not 255: accept a part that finished within two minutes before the Spark's recorded off time. Retry row stays with the 01 plan.
guards: Never stops anything to bring something back (noStops stays).
Never after out of memory, a quick death, or twice in 6 hours.
Never on Spark 2.
Needs one check by hand: docker ps -a on Spark 3 after a clean power-off, to read the real exit code.
kept.ownerDecision: After you power a Spark off cleanly with a model running, should that model come back by itself at power-on? The contract says yes; today's code says no.

kept.title: Why a start failed is lost at the next restart, and a code fault leaves no trace Sparkie can read
kept.gap: A failed operation's log lives only in memory: the last 50 jobs (service/src/07-jobs.mjs:16), read by operation_log, which answers 'expired' after a restart (service/src/16-actions.mjs:734). Every install, undo and watchdog restart empties it. The fleet record keeps 300 characters of the error (07-jobs.mjs:79) and the chat gets one line plus 'Its log is in Activity' (service/src/14-chats.mjs:129), a page the owner does not use. The failed container's own log is removed by the next start (07-jobs.mjs:134). For the console's own bugs it is worse: runJob keeps only e.message (07-jobs.mjs:61-63) and the handler sends e.message and logs nothing (service/src/24-handler.mjs:696-698). A TypeError inside startModel reaches Sparkie as one sentence with no function or part name, and service_logs shows 100 journal lines that do not contain it (service/worker.py:222).
kept.failure: GLM fails to start at night; the watchdog or an update restarts the console; next morning you ask 'why did GLM fail?'. Result: operation_log says expired, fleet_events has 300 characters, and the retry has already removed the container. Or: a patch breaks plan(); every start answers 'Cannot read properties of undefined'; Sparkie cannot tell which function, so a human with a terminal has to find it.
kept.ownerSays: "Why did GLM fail last night?" gets the real log lines, even after an update. "Anything wrong with your own code?" gets "start_model threw in plan() on build f9e9…, three times today."
kept.build: (1) console.error(e.stack) for any non-HttpError in the handler catch and in runJob's catch, so service_logs shows the function. (2) On a failed job, write its masked last 120 log lines and error to one state file (newest 30); operation_log falls back to it. (3) Change 'Its log is in Activity' to name operation_log. No faults list.
guards: Log text is stored masked and returned as data, never as instructions (R7, R26).
One new state file, listed in architecture section 4 and in the backup; no secret in it.
No new action: fields on recent_operations and a fallback in operation_log.
runJob is not in a workflow's code list, so nothing needs validating again.

kept.title: A recipe source that reads as empty wipes the setups it gave before, and the look is stamped fresh
kept.gap: The review fix keeps earlier setups only when a source throws (service/src/11-setups.mjs:196-197). A source that changes its layout does not throw: the parsers drop what they cannot read (:72, :80, filter(Boolean)), and vLLM's source swallows network errors as 'nothing' (:86, catch(() => null), then :89). The report then says '0 found' with no error (:163), the earlier setups are dropped and the model is not looked at again for a week. No test imports service/dig.mjs (docs/architecture.md section 6, 'A recipe source'), so neither the gate nor Sparkie can tell a parser broke. The 02 analysis noted 'a source that moves returns an empty list' and proposed a daily 'what is outdated' read; the data loss in digModel was not covered and that read is not built.
kept.failure: recipes.vllm.ai is down for an hour during the daily look, or NVIDIA renames a folder. Result: each model looked at that day loses its vLLM (or NVIDIA) setups, shows '0 found', is marked fresh, and the next start of a model never run here uses a slower setup or the engine's defaults. Nobody is told.
kept.ownerSays: "Are the recipe sources still readable?" gets "Three of four; NVIDIA's read as empty since Tuesday, so I kept what I had."
kept.build: In digModel: a source that returns 0 where the earlier look's report for that source had found more than 0 counts as failed ('read as empty; it had N last time'), so the existing keep-and-retry-tomorrow path applies. In vllmRecipeSetups: only a 404 is 'nothing'; other errors throw. When one source reads empty for every model in a daily round, one notice: 'NVIDIA's recipes read as empty today; its layout may have changed.' Add test/dig.test.mjs: one saved sample file per source through dig.fromNvidia, dig.fromSparkrun and dig.fromVllmRecipes; it fails when a parser returns null for a good sample. Test (workflows.test.mjs): a second look with an empty fixture keeps the first look's setups and its date.
guards: Commands are still read by code and vetted by dig.vetSetup; nothing is written by a model.
digModel is in find_setups' code list, so that workflow needs one validation run (the next look counts).
Tests still never reach the web: samples are files.

kept.title: A model that is running but has stopped answering is never noticed
kept.gap: The watcher reads Docker's state only (service/src/19-watcher.mjs:45-48), should_be_running calls a running container 'running' (service/src/20-desired.mjs:46), and the silent check exists for the brain alone (service/src/20-heal.mjs:141-156). Whether a model answers is checked only when someone calls running_models (service/src/16-actions.mjs:482-484). The 01 analysis skipped automatic restarts of hung models (a false restart of GLM costs 12 minutes); that ruling stands, but it also left the owner untold.
kept.failure: GLM across Spark 3 and 4 deadlocks after a cable hiccup. Docker says both parts run. Result: no event, should_be_running says running, your agents get timeouts from /v1, and you find out from them. Then 'restart it' answers 'already running' (service/src/17-changes.mjs:571).
kept.ownerSays: "Is everything that should run actually answering?" Or unasked in the next reply: "GLM is running but hasn't answered since 14:02."
kept.build: Telling only, no restart. In watchHeld (20-desired.mjs, already every minute): for each should-run entry that runs and started over 30 minutes ago, one HTTP GET to its own server (servedModel, 5 seconds; the engine's health path where it has one). After 10 minutes of failures: state 'not answering' in desiredNow, one notice ('GLM is running but hasn't answered for 10 minutes. Say stop and start it to restart it.'), cleared when it answers. Test (desired.test.mjs): a mock model that stops answering its port shows 'not answering' and one notice; nothing is stopped or started.
guards: Never restarts or stops anything by itself.
One GET a minute per model over HTTP, no SSH; a busy model that answers its list call is not flagged.
One notice per silence, not per minute (events stay rare, R23).
Not checked on a Spark: whether a hung vLLM engine still answers /v1/models; pick the path with one trial.
kept.ownerDecision: Keep hung models as tell-only (recommended), or let healing restart one after 10 silent minutes at most twice in 6 hours?

kept.title: A worker.py-only patch still installs with every start and crash restart switched off
kept.gap: worker.py is hashed into every workflow's version (service/src/18-workflows.mjs:14, :66) but not into the build id (service/src/01-setup.mjs:19; deploy/host-on-portal.sh:48), and the installer compares only the lock's build (deploy/host-on-portal.sh:56-57). The map records this as R29 'Today' and the 04 report as 'partly' fixed. It matters more after handoff: worker.py is the file a self-made fix to probes or logs would touch, and the result (starts refused, healing skipping with 'hasn't passed Spark Console's tests', service/src/20-heal.mjs:89 and 18-workflows.mjs:259) looks like a fleet fault, not an install fault.
kept.failure: Sparkie (or anyone) edits only service/worker.py, the tests pass, the old lock still names this build, the install goes through. Result: all five workflows are 'untested'; no model can be started and no crash is healed until undo_update or a new one-hour lock run.
kept.ownerSays: "Install it" after a worker fix is refused with "run the full test first", instead of quietly switching every workflow off.
kept.build: Add worker.py to the build id in the three lists the map already names (service/src/01-setup.mjs:19, deploy/host-on-portal.sh:48, test/fleet.test.mjs:25). kept.title: A service that Docker restarts by itself can crash-loop without the watcher ever noticing, or flood the record when it does
kept.gap: The watcher only re-inspects a container when its 'id:state' pair changed since the last minute (service/src/19-watcher.mjs:95-100). A container with a restart policy (typical for hand-started Open WebUI, databases, ComfyUI: --restart always/unless-stopped) that dies and is back in 'running' before the next look keeps the same id and state: no inspect, no 'crashed' event, and startedAt/exitCode stay stale so workloads reports the old run time. When the look happens to catch 'restarting', each flip writes a crashed and a started event (19-watcher.mjs:152-158); the in-memory record that fleet_events and fleet notes read holds 500 events (19-watcher.mjs:30), so a few hours of looping pushes out everything else, including the Spark offline/online history that the dark-period reading uses. The stand-in docker has no restart policy, so no test can see either case.

It writes the intent where it already belongs: `docker update --restart unless-stopped <name>` (or `no`), through runAction, a claim, a job and run (R11). Docker then brings it back after a power cycle with no console state at all, so it survives console restart, update, rollback, brain swap and loss of the state folder. Add a read-only notice when a Spark comes back: non-model containers that were running before it went off, are not now, and have restart 'no'. Fix restart_model's description (drop 'or workloads'). Test (heal-more or fleet test, stand-in docker): a hand-started service on spark3, keep_running, Spark off then on, it is running again and the notice names only the ones not kept; fails today.
guards: Refuse Spark 2 (nothing starts there but the brain), protected names (qwen-recipe-*, spark.protect), console models and Sparkie's own container
Never creates, removes or re-runs a container; only changes the restart policy of one that exists
A GPU container is kept only after the owner's words say so; the notice says it may be what froze the Spark
Passkey rule for things started outside Spark Console still applies to stopping (22-passkey.mjs stopsOutside)
kept.ownerDecision: May Sparkie set a restart policy on containers you started by hand on Spark 3/4 (yes makes them come back after power-on by themselves)?

kept.title: A Spark going off or on is not saved, so a console restart shows an old 'last seen' and logs a false 'went offline'
kept.gap: noteSparkStates updates lastSeenAt, online and the new last readings only in memory (19-watcher.mjs:204-215). knowledge.json is written only when a container changed or a model was learned (19-watcher.mjs:232), and an off Spark's look returns before anything changes (19-watcher.mjs:127). So the file can hold online:true and a lastSeenAt from the last container change, days old.
kept.failure: Spark 3 runs one model for three days, the owner powers it off, then a console update restarts the service. fleet_status and spark_diagnostics now report Spark 3 'last seen' three days ago (16-actions.mjs:462, :757). The first status check sees stored online:true against offline and writes a second 'spark-offline' event stamped with the install time. Sparkie answers 'when did Spark 3 go off?' with the install time. cameBack() (20-heal.mjs:26-38) measures the off time from that false event, so a power-on within 90 seconds of an install is not treated as a power cycle and what should be running there is not brought back.

Test in state.test.mjs: mark spark3 offline with no container change, restart the service, expect lastSeenAt within a minute of the real off time and exactly one spark-offline event; fails today.
guards: Save only on a flip, not every 30-second status check
A failed save logs and carries on, as today

kept.title: The watcher's record is wiped silently if its file is unreadable, and thins out after a log rotation
kept.gap: knowledge.json, links.json and heal-tries.json are read with readJson, which turns any bad file into null (19-watcher.mjs:10, 06-links.mjs:92, 18-workflows.mjs:241), while other state uses readKept, which sets the file aside and posts a notice (03-identity.mjs:10-26; tested for three files only, test/state.test.mjs:170-198). events.jsonl is rotated to .1 at 5 MB (19-watcher.mjs:32) but start-up reads only the new file (19-watcher.mjs:15). writePrivate leaves `<file>.<pid>.tmp` behind when the write fails (03-identity.mjs:29-31), and the event append swallows its error (19-watcher.mjs:31-35).
kept.failure: knowledge.json is damaged (disk full during a copy, a bad restore). On start the record becomes empty with no notice: every stopped or removed container's start command, mounts and ports are gone (the only record of how a hand-started service was run), first-look mode hides that minute's changes, and every hand-started model is 'learned' again with duplicate events. With heal-tries.json gone, the two-restarts cap starts from zero. Separately: right after a rotation plus a restart, fleet_events has almost no history, the 'cut off by a restart' report misses operations whose start is in .1, and cameBack() finds no offline event, so a powered-on Spark's models are not brought back. On a full disk each minute's failed save leaves another partial .tmp file, which the daily copy then carries to Spark 3.
kept.ownerSays: Did any of your state files fail to load, and what was set aside?
kept.build: Two changes: readKept in try/catch for knowledge.json (so a bad file is set aside with a notice), and prepend the tail of events.jsonl.1 when the new file has under 500 lines. Drop links.json and the tmp cleanup.
guards: readKept throws on non-ENOENT read errors; at module load that must fall back, not stop the service
Set-aside copies are kept, never deleted by the console

kept.title: The dev-box layer (VS Code servers, their tunnels, the workspace files) has no home in the repo, the backups or Sparkie's tools
kept.gap: The editors are the old portal's units: `spark-portal-editor.service` on each Spark and tunnel services on Spark 2 for Spark 3 and 4, 'not touched' at cutover (docs/retire-portal.md:104-110).
