Files live in ~/workspaces and ~/.local/share/spark-portal/workspaces (same lines), outside the state folder that the daily copy takes (25-backup-and-start.mjs:12). The health check reads only the Spark's own unit (service/worker.py:134), not whether Spark 2's tunnel port answers. Restart is a page-only route (24-handler.mjs:364 with 12-status.mjs:165-173), files have no action at all, and the error text says 'Restart it from the Spark's menu' (21-editor.mjs:72). kept.build: Keep only: (1) the installer says loudly when it falls back to code-server's Node, and any 'retire the editor' change must install a real Node first; (2) ask the owner whether workspace files join the daily copy. The rest is works/ow-5 and add/ow-4.

The editor stays owner-only, browser-only, passkey-fresh from the internet (R-rules for /connect)
No port forwarding through the console (21-editor.mjs:17-19 stays)

kept.title: 'Becomes a one-click recipe once the owner approves it' has no approval path, and the candidate lives only in the watcher's file
kept.gap: learnRecipe stores the candidate on the workload entry in knowledge.json and says it waits for the owner's approval (19-watcher.mjs:176-188); docs/agent-door.md:155 repeats it. kept.title: A crashed service is seen, never brought back, and Sparkie has no tool to restart it
kept.gap: The watcher records every container and writes a crashed event for any kind (service/src/19-watcher.mjs, watchSpark, the 'crashed' branch). Healing then drops it on the first line: maybeHeal returns unless kind is 'model' and it was started by the console (service/src/18-workflows.mjs:248). The should-run list only takes console model jobs (service/src/20-desired.mjs:17-20), so the power-on bring-back in healPass never covers a service. stop_model and restart_model refuse anything that is not a console model (service/src/17-changes.mjs:537, :568). The earlier plans design run_workload, stop_workload and keep_running (docs/analysis-2026-11-11/05-all-in-one-building-blocks.md, block 1) but none is built, and they do not say that healing must cover adopted containers before the full runner exists. guards: Refuses Spark 2 until the owner decides on CPU-only work there
Refuses protected containers and anything with the model label

kept.title: When the console's own code breaks, Sparkie cannot find the error or read the code
kept.gap: Errors in the console's timers and requests go only to the journal: process.on('unhandledRejection') just prints (service/src/25-backup-and-start.mjs:86) and loops print their own (for example 'Self-healing: ...' in service/src/20-heal.mjs healPass). Nothing counts them or turns a new one into an event, so a timer that throws every minute is silent. Sparkie's only window is service_logs, which takes no filter (service/src/16-actions.mjs, service_logs input is spark and service only) and returns a fixed 100 journal lines (service/worker.py:222). On a busy console an error scrolls out in minutes. No action reads ~/spark-console-src (AGENTS.md:39 says the source is there), and file reads exist only as a page route (service/src/24-handler.mjs:367). The earlier plans cover installing (update_console) and defer editing (change_console); neither gives Sparkie the read-only step that comes first: notice, locate, quote the lines.
kept.failure: A change makes fabric() or the watcher throw on every round. The page still answers. 'Is anything wrong with you?' gets 'no' because the last 100 log lines are request noise; finding the stack trace and the function needs a person with journalctl and an editor.

kept.build: Piece 1 with the first stack lines kept in the in-memory tally (so the function name is there without the journal), shown in sparkie_setup. Piece 3 as one read-only action, built with update_console in the self-update area. Drop the service_logs change.
guards: Read-only: no write, build or install from these
Paths resolved and checked to stay inside the source folder; no symlink following
Log and source text is data, never the owner's words
The first-seen notice is an event in the page chat only, never sent to Telegram unasked
Counts toward the planned tool cut: fold console_source into one read, not two tools
kept.ownerDecision: May Sparkie read its own source and docs through an action (reading only)?

kept.title: The Workload runner has no rule for who restarts, how big logs get, or what is kept when a job ends
kept.gap: The Workload spec lists image, command, port, caps and a check but not three things healing depends on. (1) Who restarts: the console's models use no Docker restart rule and are healed by the console (service/src/05-library.mjs:361-362), the brain uses unless-stopped (service/src/13-main-model.mjs:128). If services copy the brain, Docker restarts them behind the console's back (see ow-heal-3) and, after a power-on, before the models, so a model's bring-back can be refused for room (restartChecked's room check, service/src/17-changes.mjs:576-583). (2) Logs: no docker run the console writes sets a log size cap (no --log-opt anywhere in service/src), so a chatty service fills the disk unless the Spark's Docker daemon caps it, which nothing checks. (3) A job's result: a script container that exits is just a 'stopped' or 'crashed' event; its exit code and last lines are not kept anywhere once it is removed.
kept.failure: A service started by the new runner logs 2 GB a day. Weeks later the disk on Spark 3 is full and every model start fails at pull or load; or after a power-on Docker restarts a GPU service first and healing skips the model with 'doesn't have room'.
kept.ownerSays: Why did the import script fail? / What is filling Spark 3's disk?
kept.build: Two lines of text: add 'log size caps, a memory cap, no GPU by default, exit code and last lines kept for a job' to the 'A new kind of workload' row in docs/architecture.md:227 and to block 1 in 05-all-in-one-building-blocks.md. Note: sticky-1 deliberately uses Docker's restart policy for adopted non-GPU services; say so in the same row.
guards: Do not add the log flags to dockerRunCommand in the same change: that changes both start workflows' versions and needs its own lock and validation run
Order after a power-on: models first, then kept services

kept.title: A long script or batch dies with every console restart and waits for a person to start it again
kept.gap: Operations live only in memory (docs/architecture.md section 4: 'Operations and claims ... Survives a restart: no'). On stop the console waits 60 seconds and exits (service/src/25-backup-and-start.mjs, the SIGTERM handler). After the restart the only thing that happens is a notice: 'A restart of Spark Console cut off ... Check it's running; if not, start it ... again' (service/src/19-watcher.mjs, the start-up scan near the top). The console restarts on every install, every watchdog trip and every crash. The planned run_batch runs inside the console and is 'resumable', with stop and pick-up by name (docs/analysis-2026-11-11/10-round-two-report.md, item 7); the plans' check is only that a cut-off job 'still reports'. Picking it up again by itself is not in any plan.
kept.failure: 'Run these 5,000 prompts through GLM' is at item 2,100 when an approved update installs. The run stops. The chat gets a notice. Nothing continues until the owner says 'pick up the run'.
kept.ownerSays: Did the batch survive the update? / Where is the run now?
kept.build: One sentence added to the run_batch design and its acceptance test: 'a run cut off by a console restart continues by itself once, from the next item'. Nothing to build until run_batch is.
guards: Resumes only work the owner started; never starts or stops a model to do so
One automatic pick-up per restart; a run that is cut off three times is parked and says so
Honours the owner's pause
Telegram gets the final line only, as today's tell rule says

kept.title: Sparkie cannot see or touch files, though every Spark already has a bounded file service
kept.gap: service/worker.py:326-330 already does list, read, write, mkdir, rename, delete inside a fixed workspace (personal or shared), with path checks (:332-341) and a revision check. It is wired only to the page route (service/src/12-status.mjs:150-163, 24-handler.mjs:105). No action uses it, so Sparkie cannot answer "what is in my shared folder on Spark 3" or save a result as a file. Analysis 05 says of Files "Exists: nothing ... files arrive only by scp" (docs/analysis-2026-11-11/05-all-in-one-building-blocks.md:59), which is wrong, and it plans a new ~/spark-data tree beside the existing workspace. guards: Reuses the worker's fixed roots and path checks; no new path handling in Node
File text returned to the brain is data, never instructions; reading a file marks the turn as having read outside text
save_file writes only new files or with a matching revision; overwrite of an existing file is a button
Owner only; agent keys get list only; members keep their own scope as today
Size caps: read 20 KB, write 200 KB; no binary
kept.ownerDecision: Is the existing workspace (personal + shared on each Spark) the one data home, or do you still want a separate ~/spark-data on Spark 2 as analysis 05 planned? Recommend the existing workspace.

kept.title: The dev box (VS Code on each Spark) is operable only from the page that is being cut
kept.gap: Restarting a Spark's editor exists as a job (service/src/12-status.mjs:166-176, route at 24-handler.mjs:372) and is reachable only from the page menu (public/app.js:842, :1287, :1761). On Telegram the reply says the editor opens only from the Tailscale address

kept.gap: The contract wants for every running workload 'where, its address ... its health' (docs/contract.md:231) and 'done means working: the app's page loads' (:618). `workloads` returns raw `ports` and `running` only (service/src/16-actions.mjs:812-817). kept.title: 'Write a script and run it' has no design at all, and it is most of what the coding agent does today
kept.gap: Contract tests T16 and T49 (docs/contract.md:828, :861) and section 9.2 (:613) promise scripts written and run by Sparkie; the contract itself lists 'nothing yet for ... scripts' (:941). kept.title: A throw while a turn is being set up leaves the chat "still answering" until the service restarts
kept.gap: In sparkieTurn the chat is marked as answering at service/src/14-chats.mjs:212-213 (replying.add, replyingBy +1), but the try/finally that calls finish() only starts at about :296. (:254), which calls memoryPrompt() -> memoryEntries() -> readKept(MEMORY_FILE) (service/src/20-memory.mjs:11,15). readKept throws a 503 on any read error that is not 'missing' (service/src/03-identity.mjs:14). fleetNotes also does e.at.slice (service/src/19-watcher.mjs:245) on events the loader accepts without an 'at' (19-watcher.mjs:16). kept.title: A read error on desired.json or validations.json is treated as "empty" and then written over; chats and access have the same blind spot
kept.gap: readKept was written so a failed read is 'try again, never empty' (service/src/03-identity.mjs:8-14). Two callers undo that: desired() wraps it in try/catch and returns an empty list (service/src/20-desired.mjs:9-13), and validations() does the same (service/src/18-workflows.mjs:78). Both are then used read-modify-write: desiredAfter (20-desired.mjs:25-38), markUndone (:147), recordWorkflowRun (18-workflows.mjs:86-96). chatData() treats ANY read error as a corrupt file and moves chats.json aside with only a console line, and silently replaces a valid JSON file of the wrong shape (service/src/14-chats.mjs:11-21). access.json is read with readJson (03-identity.mjs:7,33-36): unreadable means 'no owner', with no aside, no notice and no fallback. test/state.test.mjs:170-208 covers only verified, added-models, main and found-setups.
kept.failure: (a) One transient read failure (EMFILE during a burst of SSH children, EIO) at the moment a start finishes: desired() returns revision 0 with nothing running, desiredAfter writes that plus the one new model. Every other model on the should-run list and all 50 revisions are gone; nothing is set aside; undo says 'nothing to undo'; self-healing no longer brings those models back after a power cut. (b) Same for validations.json: every other workflow drops to 'not validated yet'. (c) A transient error at the first chat read after a restart renames chats.json aside; the owner sees an empty chat list and no notice. (d) access.json corrupt: every request answers 'No owner is set up', page, sessions and Telegram alike.
kept.ownerSays: A hiccup reading a file no longer wipes my should-run list or my chats.
kept.build: Only the writers: desiredAfter, markUndone, the forget route and recordWorkflowRun read strictly (let the 503 through and skip the write; log it). Lookups stay tolerant. chatData: ENOENT is empty, bad JSON is set aside with a notice, any other read error throws. Leave access.json to sticky-1. One test: desired.json replaced by a folder while a stop finishes, then put back: both entries still there.
guards: A writer never writes after a failed read
Keeping the last good owner in memory never widens access: same login, same members
Lookups stay tolerant so the page and healing never crash on a bad read

kept.title: The daily copy makes one try at one Spark, says nothing when none is on, and forgets its result at every restart
kept.gap: backupState (service/src/25-backup-and-start.mjs:6-31) picks one target: Spark 3 if not known offline, else the first other Spark not known offline (:8). NODES order is spark1, spark3, spark4 (service/config.json nodes), and 'known offline' lasts only 60 s (service/src/02-ssh.mjs:22-23), so the pick can be Spark 1 (never reachable) or a Spark 3 that is off but not yet marked. There is no second try at another Spark. When no target is found (:9) no notice is written at all. The timer is 10 minutes after start, then every 24 h (:33-35), so the hour is set by the last restart. lastBackup lives in memory only and is shown only by /health and one line on the page's Agents tab (24-handler.mjs:56, public/app.js:4689-4694); no action, /status or Sparkie note reads it. The notice says 'it tries again tomorrow' (:26). tarCode is read when the far side closes (:17-25); if tar's close comes later a failed tar counts as ok. A failed tar still has its short file moved into place (:13).
kept.failure: The owner powers Sparks 3 and 4 down at night (their rule) and the service last restarted in the evening. Every day at that hour: no target, lastBackup = failed, no notice. Sparkie, asked 'is my state backed up?', has no tool that says. With Spark 3 off and Spark 4 on, the single try goes to Spark 3 or Spark 1, fails, and Spark 4 is never tried.
kept.ownerSays: Sparkie tells me when my state was last copied and where, and catches up by itself when I power a Spark on.
kept.build: About 25 lines in 25-backup-and-start.mjs: save {last try, last good} to backup.json and load it at start; never pick Spark 1; when the last good copy is older than 26 h, try again on spark-online and hourly; one notice per day when no Spark was on; run gzip -t on the .part before the mv; fix 'tries again tomorrow'. Add 'last copy' to /status. Skip backup_now, the second target and the restore tool (projects-5 already covers restore).
guards: Never copies to the brain's Spark or to Spark 1
Still excludes sockets, door/ and cloud.json; secrets.json stays outside
One notice per failed day, not per retry

kept.title: Docker not answering on an online Spark reads as "nothing is there"
kept.gap: Three scans hide a failed docker call with 2>/dev/null and still end with exit 0. Inventory: service/src/05-library.mjs:36 and :39 print no deploy/ext lines, the script ends on printf, so 05-library.mjs:85 sets online=true with deployments=[]. Watcher: service/src/19-watcher.mjs:97 pipes docker ps into a while loop (exit 0), 19-watcher.mjs:127 passes, and 19-watcher.mjs:163 marks every known container on that Spark state 'removed', running false, with a 'removed' event each. Healing then reads that empty list: service/src/20-heal.mjs:54 says down, gone=[] so the power-on settle branch is skipped, and for a two-Spark model 20-heal.mjs:81 returns "a part stopped (its part is gone)". service/src/20-desired.mjs:51 tells the owner "its container is gone". The stand-in docker (test/mock/bin/docker:14) can fail fast with ~/.mock/stall, but no test uses a short stall against inventory or the watcher (only test/state.test.mjs:228, a 40 s freeze).
kept.failure: Spark 4 boots, or its Docker daemon restarts for an update, or the user loses docker group rights. SSH answers, docker ps fails fast. Within a minute: fleet_events gets "sc-X removed on spark4" for every container, then "created/started" when Docker is back; running_models and workloads say nothing runs there; should_be_running says "its container is gone" and posts the held notice; for a model across Sparks 3+4 healPass stops the healthy part on Spark 3 (20-heal.mjs:101-105) and uses one of its two tries in 6 hours, before the 2-minute settle. A crash that happens in that window is recorded as 'removed' then 'created', so maybeHeal (19-watcher.mjs:156) never runs for it.
kept.ownerSays: Why does Spark 4 show nothing running? -> "Docker on Spark 4 isn't answering right now; what I last saw there was ..."
kept.build: One marker line, three readers. In INVENTORY_SCRIPT and watchScript print 'docker\tok' only when `docker ps` itself exits 0 (run it once into a variable, then loop over it). inventory(): add dockerOk per Spark. watchSpark: return false when the marker is missing (same as r.code !== 0). healReason: return null when any Spark of the entry has dockerOk false. desiredNow: why = "Docker on Spark N isn't answering". running_models/models_on_disk: add couldNotRead: ['spark4: Docker'] . No new tool. Test (fleet.test.mjs or heal-more.test.mjs): write ~/.mock/stall = 1 on spark4 with a pair on the desired list; without the fix the test sees 'removed' events and a 'healing' event; with it, neither, and should_be_running says Docker isn't answering.
guards: A Spark with Docker down is never treated as a Spark with no containers
Healing never acts on a scan that could not read Docker
The marker never changes the script's exit code, so the sysfs readings line still arrives

kept.title: The setups refresher stamps a failed first look as fresh, and one dead source makes it re-read the same 20 models forever
kept.gap: service/src/11-setups.mjs:197: `at = failedSources.size && earlier?.at ? earlier.at : now`. With no earlier look, a look where a source failed is stamped now, against the comment at :193-194 ("isn't stamped as fresh"). With an earlier look, `at` never moves while any source keeps failing, so the model is stale every day. The daily pass takes the first 20 stale models, on disk first then by rank (11-setups.mjs:233-235); the catalog has 80. Also 11-setups.mjs:86 swallows every vLLM-recipes error (`.catch(() => null)`), so that source can never count as failed: an outage reads as "0 found", the look is stamped fresh, and that source's earlier setups are dropped (kept only when failedSources.size, :196). A source fails for good when a community repo is renamed or its main branch moves (ghFiles throws, :59-60) or PyYAML is missing on Spark 2 (:71, :80).
kept.failure: Spark Arena's repo is renamed in January. From then on every model's look has one failed source. Week 1: models never looked at get stamped fresh with a source missing. After that: all 80 are stale every day, the same top 20 are re-read daily, the other 60 are never refreshed, and each daily look still writes its events. Nothing tells the owner a source is gone. Separately, recipes.vllm.ai down for one morning removes vLLM's setups from every model looked at that day, for a week.
kept.ownerSays: "Are the setups up to date?" -> "Yes, all read this week, except Spark Arena, which has not answered since the 3rd."
kept.build: In digModel's write: keep `at` only for a look with no failed source (null on a failed first look) and add `triedAt: now` always. setupsStale(id) = at older than 7 days AND triedAt older than 1 day. Order the daily pass by oldest triedAt after on-disk. Remove the `.catch(() => null)` at :86 for anything but a 404 so the vLLM source reports its error. One notice event when the same source has failed for 3 daily passes (one line, not a new tool). Test (workflows.test.mjs or a setups test with SPARK_CONSOLE_DIG_FIXTURE pointing at a file with bad JSON): first look leaves at empty and triedAt set; a second daily pass picks different models. Both fail today.
guards: A look with a failed source is never marked fresh
Every Recipes model gets looked at, even while a source is down
A source that is gone is said once, in plain words

kept.title: Docker not answering on a Spark reads as 'every container was removed'
kept.gap: The watcher's script hides Docker's failure. service/src/19-watcher.mjs:97 runs `docker ps -a ... 2>/dev/null | while ...`; the script preamble sets no pipefail (service/src/01-setup.mjs:90), so the script ends 0 with no `ps` lines. watchSpark only checks `r.code !== 0` (19-watcher.mjs:127), then marks every known container on that Spark `removed` and writes a `removed` event for each (19-watcher.mjs:161-166). When Docker answers again they come back as `created`/`started` (19-watcher.mjs:151), never `crashed`, so maybeHeal is never called. The inventory hides it the same way (service/src/05-library.mjs:36), so should_be_running says 'its container is gone' (service/src/20-desired.mjs:51). For a pair, healReason sees zero parts and returns 'a part stopped (its part is gone)' (service/src/20-heal.mjs:54, :79-81); bringBack marks a try before it acts (20-heal.mjs:91-92). The worker already reports `dockerAccessible` (service/worker.py:151) but nothing in healing reads it. The stand-in docker (test/mock/bin/docker) has no 'daemon down' mode, so no test can see this.
kept.failure: Docker restarts on Spark 3 (a package upgrade, `systemctl restart docker`, the account dropping out of the docker group) while models run. Within a minute: one 'removed' event per container, Sparkie's fleet notes say they were removed, held entries say 'its container is gone'. A pair on the should-run list gets two start attempts that both fail at `docker run`, which uses up 'twice in 6 hours'; when Docker is back nothing heals it. One-Spark models killed by the Docker restart are never seen as crashed.
kept.ownerSays: Why did Spark 3's models stop? -> 'Docker stopped answering on Spark 3 at 14:02 and came back at 14:05; GLM was not running after that.'
kept.build: In watchScript (19-watcher.mjs:95-100) capture the listing first: `ps=$(docker ps -a ...) || { printf 'nodocker\t1\n'; exit 0; }`, then loop over `$ps`. In watchSpark, a `nodocker` line means: change nothing, return false, and write one notice per outage ('Docker isn't answering on Spark 3'), cleared when it answers. Add the same marker to the inventory script (05-library.mjs:36) as `dockerOk:false` on the Spark; healReason and desiredNow treat that Spark like an unreachable one (20-heal.mjs:48, 20-desired.mjs:50 with the words 'Docker isn't answering there'). Test (heal.test.mjs): a new stand-in switch `.mock/docker-down` makes `docker ps`/`inspect` exit 1; assert no `removed` events, no `healing` event for a listed pair, heal-tries.json unchanged, one notice; remove the switch and assert the containers are still known as before.

Those codes are 'stopped', not 'crashed' (service/src/19-watcher.mjs:155), a one-Spark entry then returns null at 20-heal.mjs:77, and the file's own promise at 20-heal.mjs:6-7 ('a Spark the owner powered back on: what should be running there comes back') does not happen. A pair after the same clean shutdown falls into the 'a part stopped' branch instead (20-heal.mjs:78-81): it does come back, but with no 2-minute settle (20-heal.mjs:70) and without the 'it may be what froze it' guard (20-heal.mjs:71-73). kept.gap: On Spark 3 and 4 downloads run as `docker run --rm ... python3 -c snapshot_download` with no name (service/src/11-setups.mjs:392-396; the comment at :387 says neither Spark has the hf command, so this is the real path). A container started with `docker run` keeps running when its client dies. A console restart mid-download does the same, and the 'cut off' notice then tells the owner to start it again (service/src/19-watcher.mjs:24). The stand-in runs the download as a child of the script (test/mock/bin/docker:108-120), so it dies with it and the tests pass.

kept.title: A power cycle the console did not watch is never healed
kept.gap: Bringing models back after a power-on depends on a spark-offline then spark-online pair in the event list (cameBack, service/src/20-heal.mjs:24-36; used at :61-69). Those events are written only when the in-memory `online` flag flips (service/src/19-watcher.mjs:204-215). Two holes. (a) If the Spark went down and came back while the console was not running (a power cut that also took Spark 2, a Spark 2 reboot, linger off until the owner logs in), no pair exists, so `back` is 0 and healReason falls through to `if (!x.sparks) return null` (20-heal.mjs:77); maybeHeal also refuses exit 255 (service/src/18-workflows.mjs:341). The model is held for good. (b) The `online` flag is saved to knowledge.json only when a container changed (19-watcher.mjs:232), and the watcher returns early for an unreachable Spark (:127), so the file usually still says online:true for a Spark that is off. After a console restart the first status check writes a second spark-offline stamped now (:212): the dark period loses its real start and its last readings, and a Spark that returns within 90 s of that restart is not counted as a power cycle. A reboot faster than HEAL_OFFLINE_MS (90 s, 20-heal.mjs:21) is missed the same way. The Spark's uptime is already read every 30 s (19-watcher.mjs:209) but is used only for wording in darkPeriods.
kept.failure: Whole-site power cut. All Sparks boot; Spark 3 answers before the console's first status check. Its models show exited 255. No offline/online pair exists, so nothing comes back: every entry on the list reads 'held (it stopped when the Spark lost power or restarted)' until the owner asks for each by hand.
kept.ownerSays: "The power went out last night. What did you bring back by yourself, and what is still held?"
kept.build: Part: 19-watcher.mjs noteSparkStates only. Keep `bootAt` (now minus upSeconds) per Spark in knowledge.sparks and call saveKnowledge when `online` or `bootAt` changes. When a Spark is online and its bootAt is more than 2 minutes later than the stored one, and no spark-online event is newer than that boot, write the missing pair: spark-offline {at: stored lastSeenAt, inferred: true} and spark-online {upSeconds}. cameBack, the 2-minute settle, the twice-in-6-hours limit and the 'it may be what froze it' guard then work unchanged. Test (heal-more.test.mjs): stop the stand-in console, set a model's container to exited 255 and the Spark's uptime to 60 s in ~/.mock/status.json, start the console; expect a healing event 'came back on' and the model running. Fails today (it stays held).
guards: Only entries on the should-be-running list whose parts all exited 255, as today.
Once per boot (compare bootAt), so a console restart never replays a power-on.
The 'froze it' guard and the 6-hour window still apply; the owner's pause still stops it.

kept.title: A damaged intent file is replaced by a guess, and the notice says nothing was lost
kept.gap: State files are written by rename without a previous copy (service/src/03-identity.mjs:27-32). When one cannot be parsed: desired.json is set aside by readKept (03-identity.mjs:17-23), then watchHeld sees no file and seeds a new list from whatever is running at that moment (service/src/20-desired.mjs:64-71), so every held entry (a model on a Spark that is off) and the undo history are dropped, while the notice says 'nothing was lost' (03-identity.mjs:22). main.json: the current setup falls back silently to the first preset in config.json (service/src/13-main-model.mjs:12-15), and the same happens after an update or rollback whose config.json no longer has the saved preset id, since config.json is replaced with the code (deploy/host-on-portal.sh:181). agent-settings.json unreadable turns self-healing off and pauses agents with no notice and no set-aside (service/src/17-changes.mjs:17-22). heal-tries.json unreadable resets the limits to zero (service/src/18-workflows.mjs:321). knowledge.json unreadable makes the next look 'first', which only learns (service/src/19-watcher.mjs:10-12, :129-130), so a crash in that window is not announced or healed. The daily copy on another Spark exists (service/src/25-backup-and-start.mjs:6-33) but restoring is by hand.
kept.failure: Spark 2 loses power while desired.json is being rewritten; the file comes back empty. Spark 3 is off at that moment. On start the list is seeded from what runs now (nothing on Spark 3), so when Spark 3 powers on nothing is brought back and nothing is shown as held. The record says nothing was lost.
kept.ownerSays: "Sparkie, was any of your saved state damaged or restored from a previous copy this week?"
kept.build: Three small things. (1) writePrivate (service/src/03-identity.mjs:27-32) fsyncs the temp file before the rename, which removes the empty-file-after-power-loss case at its cause. (2) Keep a `.prev` copy for desired.json only, and have readKept fall back to it; drop 'nothing was lost' from the notice (03-identity.mjs:22) unless a copy was restored. (3) loadMainSetup (service/src/13-main-model.mjs:12-15) writes one notice when the saved setup id has no preset. Cut .prev for main.json, agent-settings.json and heal-tries.json.
guards: Never restore automatically from the other Spark's daily copy; only from the local previous copy.
agent-settings stays fail-safe: if both copies are unreadable it is still 'paused', now with a notice.

kept.title: Nothing proves the watch and heal loops are alive or that state is still being saved
kept.gap: /health answers ok:true from the request handler alone (service/src/24-handler.mjs:54-58); it carries no age for the watcher round, the heal pass or the status check. The watchdog only greps for ok:true (deploy/host-on-portal.sh:260). Both loops are guarded by a flag (`watching`, service/src/19-watcher.mjs:223-234; `healPassing`, service/src/20-heal.mjs:158-180): if one await never returns, that loop is silent for good while the page and /status look normal. Failed writes are swallowed: fleetEvent `catch {}` (19-watcher.mjs:31-34), saveHealTries `catch {}` (service/src/18-workflows.mjs:322), desired.json and knowledge.json only console.error (service/src/20-desired.mjs:38; 19-watcher.mjs:221). On a full Spark 2 disk the console keeps running from memory and presents it as saved; a restart then loses every event, list change and try count since. The watchdog keeps its own counter in the same folder (`echo "$m" > watchdog-misses`, host-on-portal.sh:261): on a full disk the file is emptied, the count restarts at 1 each minute and never reaches 3, so it never restarts anything. When it restarts the console or gives up (3 an hour, :251-252) it tells only syslog, and watchdog-restarts is never trimmed. After a restart the console cannot say why it restarted.

kept.title: Marks kept only in memory are lost on every restart
kept.gap: Several 'once' marks and short memories live in process memory and reset on each restart, update or watchdog restart. consoleStopped, the 15-minute 'stopped on purpose' mark that keeps healing from undoing a stop (service/src/18-workflows.mjs:323; read at 18-workflows.mjs:331-332 and service/src/20-heal.mjs:59), is empty after a restart, while the entry stays on the list until the stop job finishes (service/src/20-desired.mjs:17-22) and jobs are cut after 60 s (service/src/25-backup-and-start.mjs:82). heldSaid (20-desired.mjs:59) and skippedOnce (20-heal.mjs:37) are empty too, so every held entry is announced again and every skip reason is written again after each restart (20-desired.mjs:77-82; 20-heal.mjs:38-43); this fills the 500-event window that cameBack and the last-10 notes rely on (service/src/19-watcher.mjs:30, :245), and will repeat on Telegram once watches arrive. lastBackup is null until 10 minutes after each start (25-backup-and-start.mjs:5, :34), so /health reports no backup right after every update even when last night's copy is good. Durable jobs and pause counts on disk are already proposed elsewhere; these marks are not.

kept.build: Only the noise: at start, fill heldSaid from the loaded events (a 'should be running but isn't' notice for that container newer than its last started event). Leave consoleStopped in memory (works/heal-5 closes that case) and leave lastBackup alone.

kept.title: A held model can be shown with an old reason
kept.gap: desiredNow explains a held entry with the newest heal-skipped event for that container, whatever its age (service/src/20-desired.mjs:49-54), and with the watcher's stored exit code (:48, :52). A skip reason is written once and stays in the record (service/src/20-heal.mjs:38-43). So a reason from an earlier incident ('it was brought back twice in the last 6 hours already', 'a part ran out of memory') is given as today's reason for a model that was later stopped by hand or lost its container. The same stale text goes into Sparkie's fleet notes (service/src/19-watcher.mjs:248) and into the one-time notice (20-desired.mjs:82), and should_be_running stamps observedAt as now (20-desired.mjs:121) though the inventory is up to 15 s old and the watcher's view up to a minute or more. The earlier freshness review asks for 'held since when' and for off Sparks to read as off; it does not cover a wrong reason.

Thursday: someone stops it with docker stop on the Spark. should_be_running and Sparkie both say it is held because it was brought back twice in 6 hours, so the owner looks for a crash that did not happen.

kept.build: Part: 20-desired.mjs desiredNow only. Use a heal-skipped event only if it is newer than the workload's finishedAt (or newer than the last 'started' event for that container); otherwise fall through to 'it isn't running' with the exit code and finishedAt from the watcher ('stopped at 14:02, exit 0'). Return `seenAt` (the inventory's observedAt) instead of stamping now. Test (desired.test.mjs): write an old heal-skipped for a container, start it, stop it cleanly in the stand-in; expect why to contain 'stopped' and not the old reason. Fails today.
guards: View only: nothing about what gets healed changes.

kept.title: A stopped, missing or crash-looping brain stays down, and the fixed lines say it will come back
kept.gap: watchBrain acts only on a brain that is running but silent: it returns when the state is not running, or when the container started under 30 minutes ago (service/src/20-heal.mjs:145). Exited or missing: nothing happens. In a Docker restart loop (--restart unless-stopped, 13-main-model.mjs:128) the start time is always fresh, so the silence timer resets forever; RestartCount is read (13-main-model.mjs:90) and used nowhere. The owner word being built refuses a stopped brain and points at a page place: "Start it from Models" (20-words.mjs:52; same in 14-chats.mjs:305). Telegram's fixed line says "Spark Console restarts it by itself" (21-telegram.mjs:18), which is untrue for all three states. The only start is a page route (24-handler.mjs:588-592) or SSH. The earlier "brain keeper" (01-gap-analysis-plan.md, phase 1) is unbuilt, and it left the restart loop to an open-problems list that is also unbuilt.

(2) In watchBrain (service/src/20-heal.mjs:147): container exists, state exited or created, no brain job, not stoppedByOwner, for two passes: `docker start` the same container under the existing `brain:` two-in-6-hours count, one healing event; also once right after restartBrain returns. (3) restartWord (service/src/20-words.mjs:54) does the same docker start on a stopped container instead of 'Start it from Models', and TG_BRAIN_DOWN (service/src/21-telegram.mjs:18) stops promising a restart when the state is not running. kept.title: A console that crashes at start loops unseen; the watchdog misses it and restarts leave no record
kept.gap: The watchdog handles only `failed` and `active` (deploy/host-on-portal.sh:257-262). With Restart=always and RestartSec=3 (:192-193) a console that dies at start sits in `activating` between tries and never reaches systemd's start limit, so no miss is counted. When misses do reach three it restarts the same build, three times an hour, then writes to syslog (:252), which nothing reads. It never puts back the last build (planned earlier, unbuilt, and that plan's "10 minutes of failed /health" would not count here either). The service never reads watchdog-restarts (no reference in service/src). An uncaught error exits with a journal line only (25-backup-and-start.mjs:89-91); a kill at MemoryMax=512M (host-on-portal.sh:195) leaves nothing. A start is not an event; only operations it cut off are reported (19-watcher.mjs:19-26). No test runs the watchdog (architecture.md section 8).

Test with a stub systemctl in a temp home. Cut last-crash.json, clean-stop, and the stack mapping; the start notice is heal-add-6.

kept.title: Container logs never rotate: the one disk-full cause the console cannot clean up, and can prevent
kept.gap: None of the three docker run builders sets a log limit: dockerRunCommand (05-library.mjs:361), the pair's (08-cluster.mjs:301), the brain's (13-main-model.mjs:128). Docker's default json-file log never rotates, and engines log each request. The logs sit under /var/lib/docker, owned by root; the console has no sudo, so the planned free_disk cannot trim them. Free disk is read (05-library.mjs:56; diskFreeGiB in status) but nothing warns by itself until the planned open-problems list exists. On a full disk the console's own writes fail quietly (empty catches in fleetEvent, 19-watcher.mjs:31-34, and saveHealTries, 18-workflows.mjs:322).

Nothing is deleted

kept.title: Clock drift and Tailscale's own state are never sensed, though both are one field away
kept.gap: No code compares a Spark's clock with Spark 2's. Healing mixes clocks: a container's Docker start time on Spark 3 is compared with a stop time taken on Spark 2 (18-workflows.mjs:330), and budgets and windows use Date.now() on Spark 2 (20-heal.mjs:19, :69), so a clock that jumps back keeps tries "spent" and heals off. Tailscale's state is already parsed every minute (`tailscale status --json` in refreshBlocked, 23-http.mjs:72-86) but only addresses are kept; BackendState and Self.KeyExpiry are dropped. /status prints neither (20-words.mjs:18-32). The console must never fix either one, so telling is the whole job.

kept.title: Tell the owner once when healing gives up and needs them
kept.gap: When something becomes held, or the brain has been restarted twice and is still silent, the only output is a fleet event (service/src/20-desired.mjs:79-82; 20-heal.mjs:149). The owner hears only if they next ask in a chat. The Telegram design forbids unasked heal messages, and its watch kinds are: an operation ends, a Spark offline, a Spark back, a model crashed (docs/analysis-2026-11-11/09-telegram-design.md:77, :91-93). There is no kind for the one moment that needs the owner, and watches end after 7 days and fire once.

kept.title: The watchdog acts and gives up without anyone hearing
kept.gap: The watchdog writes only to the system log and two files: it logs "restarting Spark Console" and, when it stops trying, "not restarting: 3 restarts in the last hour already" (deploy/host-on-portal.sh:249-255). No part of the service reads watchdog-restarts or watchdog-misses (no match in service/src or worker.py; docs/architecture.md:150 lists them as files only). So after a hang and a restart, Sparkie cannot say it happened or why, and any operation cut off is blamed on "a restart" with no cause (service/src/19-watcher.mjs:24).
kept.ownerSays: "Did you go down today?" "Yes. The watchdog restarted me at 03:12 after 3 minutes without an answer. It cut off a download of GLM on Spark 3."
kept.build: At start, the console reads watchdog-restarts (epoch lines) and writes one notice for any restart in the last 10 minutes: "The watchdog restarted Spark Console at HH:MM because it hadn't answered for 3 minutes." sparkie_setup's console block gains `watchdogRestartsLastDay`. statusText adds the count when it is not zero. Nothing in the watchdog script changes. Test (state.test.mjs): a watchdog-restarts file with a fresh line gives one notice at start and the count in sparkie_setup.
guards: Read-only on the watchdog's files; the watchdog stays outside the console and unchanged
One notice per restart

kept.title: A reply that fails after its tools already changed something is handled as if nothing happened
kept.gap: In sparkieTurn's catch path (service/src/14-chats.mjs:359 'The model returned an empty answer', :372-378) the message is saved with error and the tools it ran, but: (a) conv.task is set only on the success path (:369), so a multi-step request loses its next step; (b) the next turn's history skips every message with an error (:194 'if (m.error) continue'), so Sparkie cannot see that it started a stop or a start; (c) Telegram answers any errored reply with no text as TG_BRAIN_DOWN, 'Sparkie's model isn't answering. Spark Console restarts it by itself' (service/src/21-telegram.mjs:18, :278), which is false when the brain answered and a change is under way. No test covers an empty final answer (grep 'empty answer' in test/ finds nothing); test/mock/model.mjs always writes closing text.

Round 2: Qwen with thinking on returns only reasoning and no content (or the brain is quiet for 5 minutes, or answers 400). The answer was cut off; the result will be posted here.'). 2) In the history loop keep an errored message when it has tools (send its content plus one line naming the tools and outcomes); still skip errored messages with no tools. 3) In tgTurn send TG_BRAIN_DOWN only when message.tools is empty; otherwise send the fixed line. kept.title: Multi-step requests still stall: the audit's row 2 is unfixed, and three cases were missed
kept.gap: docs/analysis-2026-11-11/04-wrong-as-wired-report.md row 2 (operation ends before the reply; owner types anything; no retry) is still in today's code: postResult schedules continueTask only if conv.task is already set (14-chats.mjs:136), conv.task is set only when the turn ends (:369), continueTask gives up for good while the chat is replying (:148), and any owner message clears the task (:208). Missed by that row: (1) when the first change comes back as a question, outcome is not 'started', so no task is kept (:369) and runChoice (:81-118) never sets one: a request that needed one button press loses its 'then' step. (2) A typed 'yes' clears the task at :208 before the yes-presses-the-button path at :226, while a pressed button keeps it; on Telegram typing is the normal way. (3) Agents never get a carry-on (:369 '!agent'), yet the same system prompt tells Sparkie results are posted 'so don't wait for them' (:50) and ask_sparkie's description promises nothing about asking again (20-mcp.mjs:70). test/sparkie-more.test.mjs:74-92 passes because the stand-in brain answers at once and the stand-in stop is slower than the reply.

kept.title: Nothing stops a turn from sending the brain a request it will reject, and the raw 400 is what the owner reads
kept.gap: Within one turn every tool result (up to 12,000 characters, 14-chats.mjs:340) and every tool call is appended to messages and re-sent each round, with no size check (:311-350). The agent setups allow 40 rounds of 4 calls (service/config.json:216-217, 262,144-token context at :180, 32,768 reply tokens at :210): 160 results is about 1.9 million characters, several times the context. Separately, a tool call whose arguments are not valid JSON is answered with an [error] result (:326, :333) but the bad string is echoed back in the assistant message (:317 'arguments: c.args'); servers that parse past tool-call arguments reject the next request. Either way modelStep rejects with 'The model answered 400: <server JSON>' (:273), the turn ends in the catch path, the owner reads the server's raw error text, and everything looked up is gone. test/mock/model.mjs accepts any size and any arguments (its only 400 is unparseable request JSON, :145).

Until it ends the chat refuses the owner ('Sparkie is still answering in this conversation', :182) and Telegram says 'Still answering'. /pause (20-words.mjs) blocks further changes but the turn goes on reading; the only way to end it is /restart sparkie, which is refused in the brain's first 10 minutes.

kept.gap: All three config presets share container name, port and served name (service/config.json main.presets: aphex, aphex-x4, aphex-agent all use 'qwen-aphex' on 30100). The container's labels carry only spark.model=<served> (13-main-model.mjs:129), so the setup in use lives only in main.json 'current'. That file is read with readJson (:13, :19, :36-37): unreadable reads as empty, loadMainSetup silently takes the first preset (:14), and the next saveRoutes rewrites it without presets (:37; noted in R20, no fix). switchMain saves the choice only after the new model answers, which can take 45 minutes (:207, :262-266), while the restart drain is 60 seconds (25-backup-and-start.mjs:79-80). It also sets MAIN before saving (:263-264), so a failed write leaves memory and disk disagreeing. After any of these, MAIN's sampling, thinking, toolRounds and maxTokens (14-chats.mjs:255-259) and the gateway's place count (15-routes.mjs:184, 16-actions.mjs:522) come from the wrong setup. watchBrain only checks /v1/models (20-heal.mjs:141-144), so it reads as healthy. kept.title: A damaged memory or saved-workflows file comes back empty, and nothing can put it back
kept.gap: writePrivate writes a tmp file and renames it with no fsync (service/src/03-identity.mjs:28-33), so a Spark 2 power loss can leave an empty or cut-off memory.json or saved-workflows.json. readKept then moves the file aside, returns null and posts 'nothing was lost' (03-identity.mjs:16-24). memoryEntries and savedWorkflows read that as empty (20-memory.mjs:12; 18-workflows.mjs:141). The next remember or save_workflow writes a new file holding one item. No action reads the set-aside file, the release snapshots or the daily copy, so Sparkie cannot restore what it was taught; the daily copy also needs Spark 3 or 4 to be on (25-backup-and-start.mjs:8-10). On a full disk writeFileSync throws and leaves a partial <file>.<pid>.tmp behind, one per process id.

kept.build: In 03-identity.mjs only. writePrivate: fsync the tmp file before the rename, copy the current good file to <file>.prev first, and remove the tmp file if the write throws. readKept: when the file does not parse, set it aside as now, then return <file>.prev if that parses, with a notice 'memory.json was damaged; using the copy from before the last change'. Neither function is in a workflow's code() list, so nothing needs validating again. Test in test/state.test.mjs: write two memory lines, truncate memory.json to zero bytes, call memory; it fails today (empty list) and passes with the first line back and the notice in fleet_events.
guards: Never fall back when the file is simply missing (ENOENT stays empty), so a forgotten last line does not come back.

kept.title: Telegram's loop can stop for good, and its 'brain down' line promises a restart that may not happen

kept.title: The real worker.py is never run by the suite; the stand-in is a hand-kept copy
kept.gap: On the stand-in fleet the service runs test/mock/worker.py instead of service/worker.py (test/start-mock.mjs:153; service/src/12-status.mjs:5). The real worker (592 lines, runs on every Spark, hashed into every workflow version at 18-workflows.mjs:14,67) is reached only for workspace-files (test/mock/worker.py:18-21). Status, workloads, diagnostics and logs are faked with fixed fields and fixed 2026-11-04 timestamps (test/mock/worker.py:26-40). A renamed or dropped field in the real worker (memoryFreeGiB, diskFreeGiB, uptimeSeconds, the sysfs readings being built now) passes the gate and breaks placement, the 8 GB rule and dark-Spark detection only on real hardware. Same class of stale copy: test/README.md lacks api, heal-more, heal-newer, intent and sparkie-more tests, still says 22 and 25 tools (lib.mjs and change.test.mjs:101-120 say 24 and 37) and '4-5 minutes'.
kept.failure: Sparkie edits worker.py to add a reading and renames a key. All tests pass, the lock is written, the install goes in, and fleet_status shows no free memory for every Spark, so every start is refused.
kept.ownerSays: Does the worker on the Sparks still report everything you rely on?
kept.build: One Linux-only test in fleet.test.mjs: run service/worker.py with action status under a stand-in HOME and assert every key the service copies in cleanStatus (12-status.mjs:47-60) is present. Fix README numbers by hand with T1; no generated table.
guards: The real worker is run read-only against stand-in commands; never on a real Spark from the suite

kept.title: The gate cannot pass on Spark 2, and Sparkie can neither run it nor read its result
kept.gap: Notices: no. Fixes itself: no. Needs a human: every time. The planned deploy/gate.sh and update_console (docs/analysis-2026-11-11/01-gap-analysis-plan.md phase 3) are not built: deploy/ has no gate.sh and no action runs tests (test_changes is the real-Spark validation tap, service/src/18-workflows.mjs:452). The Linux blockers the fast-gate plan listed are all still open: stand-in Sparks read the real /proc/meminfo (service/src/05-library.mjs:52, :335; 13-main-model.mjs:105), start-mock.mjs never sets SPARK_CONSOLE_RELEASES so a test on Spark 2 reads the real releases folder (18-workflows.mjs:444; test/start-mock.mjs:148-169), ports are freed before they are bound (start-mock.mjs:74). Pieces the earlier plans miss: (a) lock.mjs prints with stdio inherit and keeps nothing (test/lock.mjs:25), so an hour of output is the only record and the brain cannot read it; (b) there is no way to run only the files near a change and get a short answer; (c) the eval has the same Linux blockers because it uses startMock (test/eval.mjs:57).
kept.failure: After handoff Sparkie edits a part on Spark 2. It has no tool to run a test, so it cannot prove the change, cannot write the lock, and host-on-portal.sh refuses the build (deploy/host-on-portal.sh:26, :57). The owner must go back to the Mac and Claude Code.
kept.ownerSays: "Run your tests on the heal code and tell me what failed." / "Run the whole gate tonight."
kept.build: After T1 and the record exist: one owner-only job action run_tests {files?}, names from the fixed test/*.test.mjs list, run under nice in ~/spark-console-src, answer read from the record. Only a full run through lock.mjs writes the lock. It must start outside the service's cgroup (systemd-run, as undoUpdate does) so a console restart does not kill an hour of gate.
guards: run_tests takes file names from a fixed list of test/*.test.mjs, never a command
runs in ~/spark-console-src only, with the stand-in PATH; never touches the installed service or its state
only lock.mjs writes the lock (R22); run_tests on a subset never writes it
not offered to agents or workflow steps; owner's words only
kept.ownerDecision: May the gate run on Spark 2 beside the brain (under nice, about 2-5 minutes after the fast-gate cuts), or only when you ask?

kept.title: Nothing checks the real Sparks after an install except a human trying sentences
kept.gap: Notices: partly (watchdog sees a dead /health; the validation tap covers start, stop, restart on one small model). Everything else is proven only on stand-ins that differ in kind: ssh and scp are stubs that always fail, so the real ssh command line and the `timeout -k` guard never run (service/src/02-ssh.mjs:10-14; guard is `!ALL_LOCAL`); the 592-line service/worker.py is replaced by a 49-line stand-in (test/start-mock.mjs:157), so status, logs, sysfs and systemctl reads are untested; docker, curl, nvidia-smi, df, free are bash stand-ins (test/mock/bin). AGENTS.md step 8 ("check the change the way the owner would use it") and the gap plan's "twelve fixed sentences on the real Sparks" are done by Claude Code by hand. update_console's four planned checks cover only the console (build, owner, keyless refused, a chat turn).
kept.failure: A worker.py edit returns a field under a new name. Every test passes (the stand-in worker still returns the old one). After install fleet_status shows no temperatures and dark-Spark findings go blank; nobody knows until the owner asks why.
kept.ownerSays: "Check yourself." / "Did the update break anything on the Sparks?"
kept.build: One read action self_check: runs every read action that needs no argument through runAction as the owner, plus the real worker status per online Spark, and checks for no error and a fresh observedAt. Run it when the owner asks, and once at start when the build differs from the last build checked; the result is one notice. No timer, no button, never goes back by itself.
guards: read actions only; a self_check that changes anything fails R11
skips Sparks that are off and says so instead of failing
the expected-fields list ships with the code and is covered by build.test so it cannot drift from the actions
kept.ownerDecision: On a failed check right after an install: only tell you with a Go back button, or go back by itself?

kept.title: A flaky failure looks the same as a real one, and the known flaky spots are still in
kept.gap: Notices: no. lock.mjs is all-or-nothing with no retry and no history (test/lock.mjs:25-29). The fast-gate plan (07-fast-gate-plan.md section 3) named a dozen races; they are still there: `sleep(300)` after SIGTERM (test/state.test.mjs:143), a 20 s x SLOW stall limit (test/across.test.mjs:22), 25 bare sleeps across the suite, the agent door's fixed 50 s give-up that SLOW cannot stretch (service/src/20-mcp.mjs:222). The README itself warns that one timeout causes odd later failures in the same file. On Spark 2 the suite will share the machine with the brain, so timing gets worse, not better.
kept.failure: Sparkie runs the gate at night while the brain answers an agent. state.test times out once. The gate is red, the lock is not written. Sparkie either reports a bug that is not there, or "fixes" working code, or raises SPARK_TEST_SLOW until real waits triple.
kept.ownerSays: "Which tests are shaky?"
kept.build: Do the 07 section 3 holds first. In lock.mjs a failed file runs once more alone; a pass on the rerun is written into the gate record and the lock as flaky, by name, and the approval line shows it. No flaky.json, no three-strikes notice. Whether a rerun pass may write the lock is the owner's one decision here.
guards: exactly one rerun, alone; never a third
a flaky pass is recorded in the lock and shown in the approval line, not hidden
no change to SPARK_TEST_STRICT or to any assert
kept.ownerDecision: Is one rerun of a failed file acceptable for the lock, or must every file pass first time?

kept.title: The page has no test at all, not even a syntax check
kept.gap: Notices: no. No test file reads public/app.js or any file under public/ (the only matches for "public/" in test/ are the /public/fleet API route, test/internet.test.mjs:58). The lock's fingerprint and build id leave public/ out (test/lock.mjs:16; R29 in docs/architecture.md). The page is one of the owner's two ways in. kept.failure: Sparkie adds a status line to app.js and leaves an unclosed brace. Gate green, lock written, installed. The page is blank on the owner's phone. Telegram still works, so it is not a lock-out, but the fix needs someone who can see a browser console.

Leave the 72-path route check until the REST copies are removed; the lock hash for the page is sticky/T3.

no new page features to make it testable

kept.title: Tie the real-brain eval to the action list and stamp it with the brain, so it is the bar for handoff and for every brain swap
kept.gap: The eval is the only proof that Qwen, not a script, makes the right call, and it is thin and stale. test/eval/cases.json has 16 cases, all one message, all about start, stop and lookups; none for save_workflow, run_workflow, remember, forget_memory, find_setups, test_changes, undo_update, Telegram or ask_sparkie. test/eval.mjs:44 hard-codes 5 change actions while test/lib.mjs:43-44 lists 13, and :89 counts only outcome 'started', so a wrong remember or save passes (already noted in 02-tools-and-freshness.md:306, still unfixed). The only saved result is test/eval/results-2026-11-08-partial.json: one case, one run. No full run exists. Results carry no brain model id, setup or console build (eval.mjs:130), so a score cannot be tied to a brain. The usage text hard-codes the owner's tailnet address and an SSH tunnel (eval.mjs:11,15,52). Earlier plans add cases and fix the list by hand; nothing keeps it from going stale again, and nothing makes the eval the test a new brain must pass.
kept.ownerSays: "How did your brain score on the last eval?" and, after swapping the brain, "is the new brain as good as the old one?"
kept.build: One stand-in test in door.test.mjs: every name in CHANGE_TOOLS (test/lib.mjs:43-44) appears in at least one eval case as the expected action and in one near-miss that expects no change. Add the roughly twenty cases that makes. No via field, no read-tool rule.
guards: The eval only ever runs against the stand-in fleet; it never touches a real Spark.
It never writes the lock and is not part of lock.mjs; the gate stays brain-free.
A run where the chat itself failed is not a score (kept from eval.mjs:121-125).
One writer for the results file; partial runs stay marked partial.
No second brain or judge model: grading stays by audit lines, not by words.
kept.ownerDecision: When the eval may run on the real brain (it takes brain slots; R36 keeps one for the owner's chat), and whether a brain swap is refused, or only warned, when the bar is not met.

kept.title: The gate leaves a record Sparkie can read: what ran, what failed, how long
kept.gap: test/lock.mjs:25 runs the suite with stdio inherit and writes nothing unless everything passes (:26-28). A failed gate leaves only an hour of terminal text on whatever machine ran it. Claude Code reads that scrollback today; Sparkie has no such thing. service/workflows.lock.json holds only build, testedAt and versions. Nothing in service/src reads a gate result (grep for lastGate finds nothing). So after handoff the owner cannot ask whether the tests passed, and Sparkie cannot see which test to fix or which test is slow or flaky. The fast-gate plan (07) lists flaky tests found by hand from gate logs; there is no kept history to find the next ones.
kept.ownerSays: "Did the tests pass on the last change? What failed?" and "which tests are slow or flaky?"
kept.build: In test/lock.mjs: add a second reporter (node --test --test-reporter=spec --test-reporter-destination=stdout --test-reporter=junit or a 30-line custom reporter to a file) and always write test/last-gate.json, pass or fail: tree build, start and end time, per file {ms, passed, failed}, and for each failure the test name and the first 300 characters of the assertion, masked. Keep the last 10 runs in the same file so a test that fails one run in five shows. Add one field, lastGate (date, build, passed, failed names, minutes), to the existing sparkie_setup read. The test: lock.mjs given a suite with one failing file writes the record and still writes no lock.
guards: Only lock.mjs writes the record (R22: one writer); the service only reads it.
The lock is still written only on a full strict pass; the record never counts as a pass.
Failure text is capped and passes the secret masking before it is kept.
The record names the exact build, so an old pass is never shown as today's.

kept.title: A one-command proof that a new test fails without the fix
kept.gap: AGENTS.md step 3 and architecture.md checklist item 2 require a test that fails without the change, but nothing can check it. test/start-mock.mjs:27 fixes SERVICE to service/server.mjs, so a test can only run against the tree as it is now. There is no git anywhere (the folder is not a repository), so the old code cannot be checked out. Claude Code proves it by hand: revert, run, restore. A 27B brain writing its own tests will often write one that passes both ways, and the lock would accept it, since lock.mjs:14-18 fingerprints only service/.
kept.ownerSays: "Show me the test that proves that fix." Sparkie answers with the two lines: failed on the old build, passes on the new.
kept.build: Now: one line in start-mock.mjs, SPARK_TEST_SERVICE to point a test at another server.mjs, ignored by lock.mjs. The proves tool waits until run_tests exists and is then about 20 lines over the newest snapshot (deploy/host-on-portal.sh:120-122).
guards: Read-only on the old build; it runs in the stand-in fleet's temporary folder.
Never writes the lock; lock.mjs ignores the variable (it must test the tree).
The variable only works with the stand-in fleet (SPARK_CONSOLE_ALL_LOCAL), never on the live service.
A fix for something the old build cannot even load (a new action) reports 'not comparable', not a pass.

kept.title: Replay real brain streams in the stand-in brain, so every live miss becomes a gate test
kept.gap: The stand-in brain is too well behaved. test/mock/model.mjs calls tools from patterns in the owner's words or from model-script.json rules ({match, calls}, model.mjs:34), always with valid JSON arguments (:94 only splits valid JSON in two), always finishing cleanly. The real 27B sends wrong argument names, half-finished tool calls, cut-off answers (finish_reason length), empty answers and long reasoning. The service has code for these (14-chats.mjs:289-297 reads reasoning and finish_reason), but no test can feed them. When Sparkie gets something wrong on the real Sparks, there is no way to turn that exact exchange into a test without the real brain.
kept.ownerSays: "You got that wrong yesterday; make sure it can't happen again." Sparkie adds the recorded exchange as a test.
kept.build: One new rule form in model.mjs, {match, stream: [[raw chunks per round]]}, and four hand-written rows in sparkie-more.test.mjs: a cut-off mid tool call, finish_reason length, an empty answer, a reply that is only reasoning. Each must end in a plain sentence and no change. No --record.
guards: Recordings are checked for secrets (masking) before they are saved in the tree.
A replay proves the code's handling, never the brain's choice; the eval stays the judge of the brain.
No change to existing rules or tests; the new form is additive.
Recordings stay small: one exchange each, capped in size.

kept.title: Make the stand-in docker generic before apps, jobs and dev boxes arrive
kept.gap: The stand-in fleet only knows model containers. test/mock/bin/docker keeps nine fixed fields per container (name, state, status, ours, model, protect, role, cluster, rank; docker:2), one serve port per Spark (portHolder, :32-37, port 8000), and one last-run-args file overwritten by every run (:118). A container cannot publish its own port, run as a job that exits with a code after a while, sit on its own network, or carry a memory cap; inspect prints a fixed vllm command (:185-199). The owner's goal is every workload: services, one-off jobs, fresh dev boxes, hosting. The planned Workload block's guards (own network, no host paths, no GPU or model on Spark 2, memory cap) cannot be tested on this stand-in, so each new kind would bring its own mock code or ship untested.
kept.ownerSays: Nothing by itself; it is what lets "start a Jupyter box on Spark 3" or "run this job tonight" ship with tests that prove the fence.
kept.build: Nothing before handoff. When run_workload is built, in that same change: keep each run's arguments in ~/.mock/run-<name> and answer inspect from it, record -p ports, and add the exit-after-N-seconds file for jobs.
guards: Existing behaviour and file formats stay; all 518 tests must pass unchanged.
Keep the stand-in cheap: the fast-gate plan counts about 430 processes per scan, so no new process per call.
No stand-in-only branch in service code; the service still runs the same commands it runs on the Sparks.

kept.title: A locked phone mid-reply loses the answer on the page
kept.gap: The service now finishes a turn after the page disconnects and its comment says the page shows the answer when it is back (service/src/14-chats.mjs:395-397). The page does not. In sendConsole a broken stream goes to catch: it shows the browser's raw error and deletes the partial reply (public/app.js:4036-4037). A stream that ends early only sets 'The connection closed before the answer finished' (public/app.js:4031). Neither path waits on conv.replying; only openConsole does (public/app.js:3980), and watchOps stops at once when no job is pending (public/app.js:3929). streamChat has no time limit (public/app.js:2444), so a read that hangs leaves state.chat.sending true for good, which also blocks the catch-up at public/app.js:3932 and :4084. This is report 04 row 22, rated High, still not built on the page side.
kept.failure: Owner sends a message on the iPhone, then locks it or switches app. On return: a red toast 'Load failed', the half-written answer is gone, and nothing more appears, though Sparkie finished and saved the answer. Sending again gets 409 'Sparkie is still answering in this conversation.' If the read hangs instead, Send stays disabled until the page is reloaded.
kept.ownerSays: I locked my phone while you were answering; the answer was there when I came back.
kept.build: public/app.js only. In sendConsole, when the stream throws a network error or ends without done: keep the partial reply, then run the same loop as openConsole (read chats/<id> every 2 s while replying, show the waiting dots, then draw the saved copy). Show 'Lost the connection; Sparkie is still answering' instead of the raw error. Add an AbortController to streamChat that gives up after 60 s with no bytes, and on visibilitychange. Test (needs the harness from page-2): fake fetch cuts the stream after one delta, chats/<id> answers replying:true then the saved reply; the test fails unless the reply ends up in the conversation and sending is false.
guards: Page only; no new route or action
Does not resend the message, so nothing runs twice
Keeps R25: the turn still runs once on the service

kept.gap: followServiceJob treats a single network miss or a 502 as the end of the job: public/app.js:2411 sets status 'failed' and breaks. activityJobs lets that local copy win over the service's list (public/app.js:429), so Activity keeps saying Failed until the page is reloaded. Test (page harness): fetch for jobs/<id> fails once then returns running, then completed; fails unless no 'failed' toast is raised and the final state is completed.

kept.gap: R33 says a recovery code alone is enough. (a) The Sign in button offers it only when whoami.signin is true (public/app.js:5161), and signin is false when there are no passkeys or passkeys.json cannot be read (service/src/24-handler.mjs:68), though /auth/signin/recovery works without passkeys (service/src/22-sessions.mjs:252). (b) After a recovery sign-in the page reloads at once (public/app.js:2094), which wipes the 'N codes left' toast, and the 15-minute 'add a passkey here' offer is drawn only on Access (public/app.js:4484), so a new phone never sees it. (c) Removing the last passkey says only 'changes to who has access need only Tailscale' (public/app.js:2328); it does not say that passkey sign-in from the internet, letting a device in, Telegram connect and new recovery codes all stop, and that a first passkey can then be made only on the tailnet (service/src/24-handler.mjs:196).

Test: internet.test.mjs, with no passkeys on file a recovery code still signs a Funnel browser in (pins the service half); page harness: signed-out page with signin:false and via:'internet' offers the recovery button.
guards: No gate loosened: the 15-minute window and passkey rules stay as in R33
whoami gains no new public fact

kept.title: Home's activity and notices go stale on an open page
kept.gap: The 15 s timer refreshes only status and the brain (public/app.js:5349). Jobs and notices are read once at start (resumeJobs) and once on Home when empty (public/app.js:1378), then only when the owner opens Activity or uses chat. So work started by healing, Telegram or an agent, and notices such as an automatic pause, a recovery-code sign-in or 'a passkey was added from the internet… if that wasn't you', do not appear on a page that is already open. Becoming visible again also skips them (visibilitychange calls loadStatus only).

kept.title: The brain fits the code only with search/replace edits; nothing tells the engine so, and some lines fight it
kept.gap: Measured fit (sizes from wc; tokens estimated at 3.5 characters each). Agent setup: context 262,144, output 32,768 including thinking, 40 tool rounds (service/config.json 'aphex-agent': maxTokens 32768, toolRounds 40; agentbar/run.mjs:82 passes maxTokens 32768). Reading: AGENTS.md + architecture.md + code-map.md are about 25K tokens; 16-actions.mjs (78,769 bytes) about 22K; 17-changes.mjs (56,902) about 16K; public/app.js (343,359) about 95K. All of service/src is 657 KB, about 185K tokens, so the whole service never fits beside the docs, and the generated copy service/server.mjs (657,135 bytes) eats 70 percent of the context if opened by mistake and doubles every grep hit. Writing: a whole-file rewrite of 16-actions.mjs is about 22K tokens plus thinking, at or over the 32,768 cap, and about 10 minutes at the 37 tokens a second the contract records (contract.md:779); app.js can never be rewritten whole. So the only edit shape that fits is exact search/replace on a few lines (both engines have such a tool). Line-number patches are the least reliable shape for a model this size, because it must count lines in a 5,000-line file. Search/replace has its own traps here: the model must reproduce the old text exactly, and this code has lines up to 538 characters in 16-actions.mjs (13 lines over 300), 557 in 17-changes.mjs, 2,292 in docs/architecture.md (63 lines over 300), with typographic apostrophes throughout (50 in 16-actions, 82 in 17-changes, 172 in app.js) that models tend to retype as straight ones. AGENTS.md, the file Qwen Code loads as standing context (agentbar/engines.mjs:59), says none of this. Sparkie's own chat loop is no substitute: under the default setup it has 4,096 output tokens and 6 rounds (service/src/13-main-model.mjs:8, 14-chats.mjs:255 and :259), every tool result is cut at 12,000 characters (14-chats.mjs:342), each action has 50 seconds (:330), and no action reads or edits a source file.
kept.failure: The engine greps for a function, opens service/server.mjs, and spends 180K tokens of context on it; or it rewrites 17-changes.mjs whole, the output is cut at 32,768 tokens, and the file is left half written; or its replace fails five times on a 500-character line because it typed ' for the curly apostrophe, and the 30 minutes run out.
kept.ownerSays: Sparkie, how do you edit your own code, and what won't you touch?
kept.build: Add about six lines to AGENTS.md under 'How to work': edit with the replace tool on the fewest unique lines; never rewrite a whole file; never open or search service/server.mjs (search service/src and public); copy old text from the file with its curly apostrophes; read big files by line range after grep. Add one more line the finding missed: the repo root also has a hand-written server.mjs (the local preview server, 5,427 bytes), which is not the generated service/server.mjs. Add the ignore file only after the first transcript shows which one the chosen engine reads. No doc-text test, no line-length lint, no reformatting until the long-line replay task fails.
guards: AGENTS.md stays short (contract 3.8: a rules card of about 40 lines); the block replaces words, it does not grow the page past that.
service/server.mjs stays generated and checked by the tests; hiding it from the engine must not hide it from the build check.

kept.title: One wake trigger, five silent dead ends: the chain stops and nobody is told
kept.gap: The only thing that starts Sparkie's next turn is a job ending in the same process: postResult schedules continueTask after 2 s (service/src/14-chats.mjs:136; 07-jobs.mjs runJob finally). continueTask then gives up without a word in five cases (14-chats.mjs:143-149): (a) more than 2 hours since the FIRST request (CONTINUE_HOURS, measured from task.at) - a one-hour gate plus a 45-minute model load already exceeds it; (b) 8 carry-ons used; (c) the chat is mid-answer (replying.has) - dropped, never retried; (d) the owner's pause is on - never retried when lifted; (e) the carry-on turn itself errors (brain restarting, 300 s timeout at :269/:304): sparkieTurn catches and returns an error message (:373-379), no job is running, so nothing wakes it again. On the page nothing says it stopped (stop() only speaks on Telegram, :147). The 04 report already proposed re-checking the task at turn end, result post and start-up (04-wrong-as-wired-report.md:44); that is not built, and it did not cover the caps, the pause, the errored turn or the silent stop.
kept.failure: Owner: 'fix X, run the gate, then ask me'. The gate job ends at minute 65 while the owner is asking something else in that chat (or the brain is mid-restart). continueTask returns at :148 or the turn errors. conv.task stays set, no job is left to end, and the chat sits forever on 'Done: gate finished' with no next step and no notice.
kept.ownerSays: Run the full gate on that fix and tell me when it's ready to install.
kept.build: One wakeWork(convId) called from postResult, from sparkieTurn's finish(), and from the existing 60 s loop (20-desired.mjs:86). No new timer. Clock from task.movedAt, set on each job result; keep 8 carry-ons per task; 24 h ceiling. An errored or thrown carry-on does not count, and is retried by the loop at most 3 times. Pause: the loop simply skips while halted, so lifting it wakes the work. On give-up push one notice in the chat. Leave start-up to wake-4's notice. Cut per-step caps. Tests: job ends mid-reply; brain fails once; give-up notice.
guards: Carry-on turns still act only on the owner's stored words (14-chats.mjs:237-238)
Pause still stops carry-on turns; lifting it wakes them through the sweep, not a new path
R9 breaker counts are unchanged; the sweep starts turns, never operations

kept.title: The steps that restart the console cannot report: the gate, the install and going back need a wake from start-up
kept.gap: A job is memory in the console process. On SIGTERM running jobs get 60 seconds, then the process exits (25-backup-and-start.mjs:64-73). At start-up the only trace is a fleet event and a general notice (19-watcher.mjs:18-25); nothing is posted in the chat that started it and no turn is started. Telegram alone gets 'A restart cut off ...' (21-telegram.mjs:311-320). So an hour-long gate run as a console job dies with any console restart (an install, the watchdog after 3 missed health checks, a crash). The install itself restarts the console, so its own result can never come through postResult. undo_update returns outcome 'started' with no operation id (18-workflows.mjs:468-486), so nothing wakes after it either. Today Sparkie has no gate or install action at all (contract.md:955-957 says so); when the gate-record work adds them, built as ordinary jobs they inherit this hole.
kept.failure: Sparkie starts the gate as a job. At minute 50 the watchdog restarts the console. The gate child is killed or orphaned, the job is gone, the chat shows nothing, and the task waits forever. Or: the owner approves, the install restarts the console, the new build comes up, and the live-check step never runs because no job ended in the new process.
kept.ownerSays: Install it, then check it live and tell me what you saw.
kept.build: Build now only the start-up half. After listen, for each chat whose task is set: post one notice by code ('Spark Console restarted; build <BUILD> is running; <operation> was cut off', or 'went back to the build from <stamp>' after undo_update), set movedAt, and let wake-1's loop run one carry-on whose prompt says the work was interrupted and to check state before acting. Write one rule into docs/architecture.md for the later self-change work: the gate and the install run outside the console, as rollback does (18-workflows.mjs:474-476), and report through a result file. Build those units with the self-change actions, not before.

What does persist: tailscale serve/funnel --bg routes (lock-api.sh:22, open-to-internet.sh:26-27), the api-locked file (23-http.mjs:45-46), and the Telegram loop, which starts at listen and retries with backoff (25-backup-and-start.mjs:52-53, 21-telegram.mjs:139-146).
