kept.title: The brain that Docker restarts by itself can hang 40 minutes on a stale rendezvous file, and one that failed to start is nobody's job
kept.gap: All four brain setups keep SGLang's rendezvous in a file inside the container: SGLANG_DISTRIBUTED_INIT_METHOD_OVERRIDE=file:///tmp/sglang-rdv (service/config.json main.presets.*.env). 20-heal.mjs:127-128 says the file 'would be found again after a restart and can hang the start', so the console's own restart deletes it first (20-heal.mjs:129-132). Docker's own restart (--restart unless-stopped, 13-main-model.mjs:128) after a host reboot, a Docker daemon restart or a crash reuses the same container, so the file is still there and nothing removes it. watchBrain then waits 30 minutes of 'loading' plus 10 minutes of silence before its clean restart (20-heal.mjs:15-16, :146-147), then the model loads again. Separately, watchBrain acts only when state is 'running' (20-heal.mjs:146). A brain left 'exited' or 'created' at boot (GPU runtime not ready when Docker starts it is a known Docker case) is never started: /restart sparkie refuses with 'Start it from Models' (20-words.mjs:54) and chat says the same (14-chats.mjs:305). From Telegram there is no way to start it. During a normal load /status says only 'running, but its server doesn't respond' (20-words.mjs:24).
kept.failure: Power returns to Spark 2. Docker starts sparkie-main with /tmp/sglang-rdv from before the cut; it hangs. No chat for about 40 minutes plus load time; if the second start also fails, healing stops after two tries (20-heal.mjs:151). Or: the container shows 'exited' after boot and stays down until the owner finds the page's Models view.
kept.ownerSays: /status  ->  'Sparkie's model: loading, started 3 minutes ago (after Spark 2 restarted at 14:02).'
kept.build: 1) Build the tmpfs fix already listed in reviews-2026-11-11.md:64, in the finding's safer form: a folder of its own (--tmpfs /rdv, env file:///rdv/sglang-rdv), since a tmpfs over all of /tmp is noexec and 64 MB by default and could break the engine. Keep the `docker exec rm` line until one live restart proves the tmpfs. 2) Cut the unattended `docker start` and the new brainStopped state. Instead let the owner's own word start it: /restart sparkie, when the container exists and is exited, runs `docker start` once under the same Spark claim. The owner asked, so no guess about who stopped it. 3) Keep the /status line 'loading, started N minutes ago' from startedAt; restartWord already computes it (20-words.mjs:56-57). Tests: words.test.mjs pins the run args and both replies.
guards: Only `docker start` of the existing brain container; never docker run or rm from healing (20-heal.mjs:124-125)
Never when the owner stopped it (console flag, or exit 0/137/143 from a manual docker stop)
Same 2-in-6-hours limit and Spark claim as today's restart
Nothing else starts on Spark 2
kept.ownerDecision: Approve one brain restart to pick up the tmpfs change (the brain's run flags are yours).

kept.title: A clean reboot or a Docker restart from an update stops models with exit 0/137/143, which healing reads as 'stopped on purpose'
kept.gap: Models on Spark 3/4 run with no restart policy (05-library.mjs:361, 08-cluster.mjs:301). Bring-back after power-on requires every stopped part to show exit 255 (20-heal.mjs:69-70), and crash healing ignores exits 0, 137 and 143 (19-watcher.mjs:157). Exit 255 is what Docker shows after a hard power loss. A graceful shutdown (owner's `sudo reboot` after an OS update, or a Docker package update restarting the daemon) signals containers first, so they end 0, 143 or 137. Every heal test models a restart as 'Exited (255)' only (test/heal.test.mjs:174-182, test/heal-more.test.mjs:84, :95). A daemon restart also never takes the Spark offline, so cameBack (20-heal.mjs:25-37) finds nothing. Whether unattended-upgrades is on, and whether it may restart Docker or change the NVIDIA runtime under a running model, cannot be read from the repo and no code reads it. 02-tools-and-freshness.md:205, :222 already rules that Sparkie never applies updates and leaves 'automatic updates on 3/4' to the owner; the missing piece is this heal gap. Needs one confirming look on a Spark after a clean reboot (`docker ps -a`).
kept.failure: Docker updates on Spark 3 at night and its daemon restarts. The model the owner left running exits 143. Self-healing does nothing, should_be_running still lists it, and the owner finds it down in the morning. Same after the owner's own `sudo reboot` for an update.
kept.ownerSays: What happened on Spark 3 last night?  ->  'Docker restarted at 03:12 after an update. GLM stopped with it and I brought it back at 03:15. A reboot is waiting.'
kept.build: Step 0, no code: after the owner's next clean `sudo reboot` of Spark 3, ask Sparkie what the fleet events recorded as the model's exit code (the watcher already logs 'stopped' with exitCode, 19-watcher.mjs:158). Only if it is not 255: in healReason accept exit 0/137/143 on the power path when the part's finishedAt (already kept, 19-watcher.mjs:119) falls inside the Spark's own offline window from cameBack (20-heal.mjs:25-37), the console did not stop it and it was not out of memory. That covers the clean reboot with no new reading. Add the Docker daemon start reading only if a daemon-only restart is then seen to stop a model. Drop the three upkeep facts from this finding. One test in heal-more.test.mjs: 'Exited (143)' with finishedAt inside the offline window comes back once; the same exit with the Spark online throughout is left alone.
guards: Never brings back a stop the console made (consoleStopped) or an out-of-memory exit
A plain exit 0/137/143 with no daemon restart or reboot stays the owner's stop
Reads only; never touches apt, Docker's service or unattended-upgrades
Bring-back never stops anything else (noStops, 20-heal.mjs:103)
kept.ownerDecision: Keep automatic OS updates on for Spark 3/4, or turn them off and update by hand a few times a year (already open in 02-tools-and-freshness.md:222).

kept.title: A console that dies after the installer's 45 seconds stays dead, silently, and the way back is written nowhere
kept.gap: The only automatic put-back is inside the install: /health must name the new build within 45 s (deploy/host-on-portal.sh:209-226). After that nothing puts a build back. The watchdog only restarts, 3 times an hour, then logs 'not restarting' to the journal and exits (deploy/host-on-portal.sh:244-257); its case covers only `failed` and `active`, so a unit sitting in systemd's auto-restart wait is skipped. reviews-2026-11-11.md:158 proposed 'after repeated failures it runs restore.sh'; it was not built. A build whose /health answers but whose chat or actions route throws passes both the installer and the watchdog (both read only /health, R30 architecture.md:208); the plan's 'four checks' live in the unbuilt update_console (01-gap-analysis-plan.md:75), not in install.sh, so a Mac or `local` install never gets them. kept.title: Step two: a time row may name one saved workflow; four things in the no-chat run path must change first
kept.gap: run_workflow can run with no chat (conv: ctx.conv || null, 18-workflows.mjs:286) and self-healing already runs changes as the owner with no chat (healOwner, 20-heal.mjs:18). Claude's notes say the Mac got its SSH key on Spark 2 on 2026-11-03; no other device is known to have one. The console must never touch SSH, so this is the owner's step, and it is written nowhere.
kept.failure: Spark 3 and 4 are off for two weeks; chats.json is damaged on Spark 2. Owner tells Sparkie 'put my chats back from the daily copy'. There is no action; the newest off-box copy is two weeks old and nothing said so; the hand recipe needs SSH, and the only device with a key is the closed Mac.
kept.ownerSays: When was my state last copied, and where? Put my chats back from Tuesday's copy.
kept.build: (1) In backupState: persist lastBackup (last try and last good copy: date, Spark) to a small state file read at start; in the no-target branch, send one notice once the last good copy is over 3 days old; run a copy when the watcher sees a Spark come back and the last good copy is over a day old. Add one line to the /status word and fleet_status: 'State last copied: <date> to <Spark>'. Tests in state.test.mjs: every other Spark off gives a notice after the age limit and /health keeps lastBackup across a restart; a Spark coming back triggers a copy. (2) Build the already-proposed owner-run deploy/restore-state.sh (list, <date>): saves current state first, stops the service, puts files back, starts, waits for /health; leaves passkeys, sessions, access and agent keys alone unless --with-sign-in; never touches secrets.json. One test that restores a deleted chat on the stand-in fleet. (3) docs/handoff.md owner steps: a second device can SSH to Spark 2 before the Mac closes (owner adds the key; the console never does), and fix sharing.md:64 to say 'from any terminal that can SSH to Spark 2' and point to recovery codes first. Cut: the restore_state action, stateCopies list, the extra local daily tar.
guards: restore_state never runs from Telegram, an agent or a workflow step: owner-only button with the passkey (PAGE_ONLY, R32).
Sign-in files (passkeys, sessions, access, agent keys) are kept as they are by default, so an old copy cannot lock the owner out or revive a removed key; secrets.json is never read or written.
The current state is saved first; a restore that does not answer /health puts that snapshot back.
Refused while any operation runs; one restore at a time (fixed systemd unit name, as undo_update does).
The script reads from other Sparks only; it changes nothing on Spark 3 or 4.
kept.ownerDecision: Restore by chat with a passkey tap, or keep it an owner-run script on Spark 2 only? And which second device (phone or laptop) will hold an SSH key to Spark 2 before the Mac is closed? You add that key yourself; Spark Console never will.

dropped.why: Same as healing/works/heal-1. Worth taking from it: the notice carries the one by-hand line (sudo systemctl restart docker), since the console has no sudo and must not touch system settings.

dropped.title: A start cut off by a console restart is never adopted or watched
dropped.why: Same as healing/works/heal-6. Its pending re-check for 45 minutes is the piece heal-6 lacked and is in the smaller version there. Use desiredAfter as the one writer (R22) rather than a direct write marked 'adopted'.

dropped.title: A long looking-up turn has no size or repeat budget and ends as a raw engine error
dropped.why: Same gap and same fix as brain-chat-3 (no size check on messages, 14-chats.mjs:311-355; raw 400 at :273). Its extras are more than needed: a repeat-call check and a 15-minute turn limit add rules to a loop that /stop (brain-chat-4) and the size budget already bound. dropped.title: A new brain setup is kept once it lists its models, with no proof it can call tools

Three 90-second calls inside startMain is the larger version and would also run on every plain brain start; BC-S4's single probe inside switchMain is enough. dropped.title: A reply that fails says so in engine words, is never retried, and a restart cuts it silently

The 30-minute reaper is not needed once that is done (every model step already has a 300-second limit, :269). Keep one small piece: /status prints 'Answers under way: N'.

dropped.title: Sparkie cannot read its own map, rules or source

The field-on-sparkie_setup form is the worse shape: sparkie_setup is in INSIDE_READS (14-chats.mjs:64), so it needs a special case to keep memory strict, and it gives one tool two unrelated jobs for a brain that already picks among 36. Take its guards (fixed allow-list, no caller path joined to a folder, no contract.md) into brain-3's tool.

dropped.title: An empty answer after tools ran is reported as a dead brain, and the carry-on is lost
dropped.why: Same gap and same lines as brain-chat-1 (14-chats.mjs:359, :369, :194; 21-telegram.mjs:18, :278). Keep its code-built line from tool outcomes (outcomeText, 14-chats.mjs:75-80) in that fix. Skip its extra model call with thinking off: it adds wait and a second way to fail, and the code-built line already says what is true.

dropped.title: A running turn cannot be stopped or steered from the chat or Telegram
dropped.why: Same as brain-chat-4 (14-chats.mjs:313, :397; 21-telegram.mjs:195, :272). Its second half, keeping the newest Telegram message typed while busy and running it later, is more than needed: once /stop exists the owner stops and retypes, and a held message that runs later on its own is a new way to surprise them.

dropped.title: Replace and forget keep no history, so a wrong save cannot be undone
dropped.why: Same gap as learning/works/learning-7 and round two's 'previous version' (10-round-two-report.md:153). The 10-item `was` list and the `removed` read flag are more than one previous version; a memory replace already states the old line in its reply (20-memory.mjs:51). Use learning-7's smaller version.

dropped.title: A saved workflow dies at the first question and cannot be carried on
dropped.why: Its facts are right, and it is the one finding that noticed the button is not shown in chat (18-workflows.mjs:275-278 passes no onQuestion). But 'from', per-step lastRun writes, a 'waiting' state and a standing yes are resume machinery the owner does not need: once learning-2 is fixed, saying the title again repeats nothing (stop answers 'already', 17-changes.mjs:541; start answers 'already'). Its parts are covered by learning-3 (smaller), learning-5 part 1 and learn-sticky-5. A saved step carrying a standing yes would undo APPROVAL_ARGS (18-workflows.mjs:155-156); do not build.

dropped.title: Sparkie is not told which routines it was taught, so a new chat can miss them
dropped.why: Same gap as learn-sticky-4 (and 01-gap-analysis-plan.md:45, :114). Its placement in fleetNotes is the right one and is taken into sticky-4's smaller version, as are the eval cases. Cut the extra sparkieCheck rule that turns a start_model matching a saved title into a button: with the names in the record the brain can pick run_workflow, and a wrong start_model already fails namesModel (16-actions.mjs:266).

dropped.title: An update can break a saved routine and nobody hears until it is run
dropped.why: Same as learn-sticky-6 (18-workflows.mjs:218-229, :151-152). Use that one. Cut the installer text hook and the 10-second timer; one notice at start is enough.

dropped.title: Sparkie does not know the saved names until it calls a tool, and "save that" is still typed from prose
dropped.why: Part 1 is learn-sticky-4. Part 2 ('save that' built by code from what just ran) is already in the first plan, built from audit.jsonl (01-gap-analysis-plan.md:27, :113), effort M, unbuilt. The finding says so itself. Its one new piece, the `when` line travelling with the name, is taken into sticky-4. Build 'save that' after the fix-firsts, as already planned; no new proposal here.

dropped.title: A saved workflow that stops half-way cannot carry on
dropped.why: Facts right (18-workflows.mjs:241-244, :264, :277-278), but 'from' is not needed. With learning-2 fixed, a second run does not repeat finished steps: stops answer 'already' (17-changes.mjs:541), starts answer 'already', lookups are harmless. learning-3's smaller version (button in chat, text naming the steps left, say the title again) gives the same result with no new input, no step-number rules and no stored state. lastRun.step is in learn-sticky-5.

dropped.title: Nothing notices when a learned thing has gone stale
dropped.why: Part 1 is learn-sticky-6. dropped.why: Same defect and same fix as channels/works/CH-2 (service/src/21-telegram.mjs:123). The extra 60 s revive timer and lastPollAt are not needed once the loop waits and continues; token-refused, not-paired and off are meant to stop, and both restart paths call tgRestart.

dropped.title: /stop on Telegram, and the next message is kept instead of dropped
dropped.why: The premise is stale: the page no longer stops a turn by closing (chatReply sets link.detached, service/src/14-chats.mjs:393; nothing sets link.gone, which is only read at :313). One turn at a time with 'send that again' is the design (R32, docs/architecture.md:211; 21-telegram.mjs:195). Stopping the answer does not stop operations already started, so /stop saves little, and a kept-message slot is new state on the channel. Cut. If wanted later, /stop alone is the piece to add.

dropped.title: The one model address passes speech and image calls too, so non-chat models are served the same way
dropped.why: The 404 for other paths is as written (service/src/15-routes.mjs:144, :156), but nothing in the console starts or lists a speech or image model: no engine, recipe field or action mentions audio or TTS (grep of service/src finds only power and sensor words). dropped.title: A failed write of the passkey counter blocks the confirmation and the sign-in it belongs to

Drop the failed-sign-in counters.

dropped.title: No check of the ways in: a door can go dead and nothing notices
dropped.why: Same build as add/AS-ADD-1 (and sticky/AS-5). One claim is off: checkRoute keeps reading funnelOn after the lock; only the socket-route test stops (service/src/23-http.mjs:57-59). The key-expiry warning is already on the backlog (docs/reviews-2026-11-11.md:109). Keep its one extra guard in AS-ADD-1: a kill timer on the two spawned tailscale commands (23-http.mjs:51, :71).

dropped.title: Lock-out warnings cannot reach the owner when the page is what broke
dropped.why: Same aim as add/AS-ADD-4. This version adds a default-on fifth kind to TELL_WHY, which goes against what tell() is documented to send (service/src/20-tell.mjs:2-7; R32 at docs/architecture.md:211; contract 13: never unasked). AS-ADD-4 does it as a watch the owner sets, which fits. Build that one.

dropped.title: From chat the owner cannot shut the internet doors or resume an automatic pause
dropped.why: /resume is works/AS-2; /lock is add/AS-ADD-6. Nothing here beyond those two.

dropped.title: Check the ways in after every install, and put the old build back if sign-in broke
dropped.why: Same gap and same file as self-fix/access-heal-1 (installer trusts /health: deploy/host-on-portal.sh:202-227). Build one check there. The before-and-after probe of signin and /auth/signin/begin is a fair second step later, but the owner whoami check is the one that prevents a full lock-out.

dropped.why: Each step is already ungated and a few taps on the page the owner is typing in: sign a device out (service/src/22-sessions.mjs:321-329), pause (service/src/22-passkey.mjs:119), disconnect Telegram (22-passkey.mjs:130-131). A lost device is rare. R34 keeps the words to look, pause and restart on purpose (docs/architecture.md:213), and unpairing Telegram in the same stroke removes the owner's one outbound alert channel at the moment they need it. If the owner still wants one word, make it only 'sign out every internet device but this one'.

dropped.why: The gap is real: test/lock.mjs:36 writes only build, testedAt and versions, and contract 6.15 (docs/contract.md:408-410) says fewer tests or a changed assertion waits for the owner. But the per-test-file hashes in the smaller sticky/CD-S4 already let the installer say 'existing test files changed: change.test.mjs' at approval, without parsing a reporter. If a count is wanted, add tests-per-file from the same junit file that sticky/CD-S7 reads.

dropped.title: Doc anchors by name, with a check, and header numbers written by code
dropped.why: Same as self-fix/cd-3. The drifted anchors it lists are confirmed, and OP_WORDS and the 22-versus-24 tool count in test/README.md:51-52 are further examples. Nothing new beyond cd-3's rewrite and name check.

dropped.title: 'Validated on the real Sparks' does not cover the shell that runs on the Sparks
dropped.why: The claim is true: START_CODE (service/src/18-workflows.mjs:15-18) leaves out inventory, run, spawnOn, PREAMBLE and q, so a change there keeps every workflow's version. But the only thing a version change buys beyond the lock is the 'validated on these Sparks' step, and the owner has decided to drop that step and keep only the tested lock (docs/analysis-2026-11-11/README.md, delegated decision 4; 01-gap-analysis-plan.md section 8 item 3). The lock already ties to the whole of server.mjs through the build id (01-setup.mjs:17-21, 18-workflows.mjs:81). Growing the hand-kept lists and adding a test to police them builds on a part that is on its way out, and costs a validation round on Spark 3 and 4.

dropped.title: The installer and restore.sh never run under a test; rollback leaves the source copy ahead
dropped.why: Same gap and same test file as tests/works/T3 (deploy/host-on-portal.sh never runs under a test), sized L where T3 does it in M. Its extra claim is true but not a fault: restore.sh puts back the page and service only (host-on-portal.sh:139-146), so after an undo ~/spark-console-src holds the undone change. That is the tree Sparkie needs in order to fix what failed; putting old source back would throw the change away. /health already names the running build and the source's lock names its own.

dropped.why: The claim is true: validations.json keeps one version per workflow and overwrites it (service/src/18-workflows.mjs:82, :92-93), restore.sh leaves state alone, so an undo drops changed workflows to needs-validation. But the owner has decided to remove the validated step altogether (docs/analysis-2026-11-11/README.md, delegated decision 4). A version history inside validations.json adds stored state to a part that is to be deleted.

dropped.title: The real-brain eval result is stale, unstamped, and needs the Mac

dropped.title: A green lock does not prove the tests were kept: the lock records nothing about the suite
dropped.why: Same facts as tests/works/T4 (the lock records nothing about the suite, test/lock.mjs:37) and tests/sticky/T3 (the fingerprint and the installer check leave out test/, public/ and config, lock.mjs:14-18, deploy/host-on-portal.sh:57). dropped.title: The undo path, the installer and the watchdog are never run by any test

dropped.title: The real-brain eval is stale, blind to 8 of 13 change actions, and tied to the Mac
dropped.why: The grader list, stale result and tunnel text are tests/works/T2; 'every change action has an eval case' is tests/add/tests-add-1; the nightly run is docs/reviews-2026-11-11.md:69. The case counts check out (16 cases; 2 start_model, 1 stop_model expect a change). Running the eval by itself after a brain switch or an install takes brain places without the owner asking; keep it owner-started.

dropped.title: A read-only live check after an install on Spark 2, reusing the door test's table
dropped.why: Same gap as tests/self-fix/tests-4 (nothing checks the real Sparks after a local install, deploy/host-on-portal.sh:348). dropped.title: The page is never tested: add a no-browser check that it loads and only calls routes that exist
dropped.why: Same as tests/self-fix/tests-7 (the page has no test; test/internet.test.mjs:58 is the only 'public/' match). dropped.title: An answer cut off by a phone lock or a dropped connection never shows up until the page is reloaded

dropped.why: Same as works/page-1 plus sticky-2 and sticky-3 (public/app.js:2444, :4036, :3980, :5336). Nothing new.

dropped.title: Attach in the composer: the one way a file reaches Spark 2 from the phone (missing piece of media-1 and run_batch)
dropped.why: Early. The file browser and its upload still exist (public/app.js:4145); retiring it is only a plan (docs/reviews-2026-11-11.md:132). dropped.title: Any new owner message in the task's chat drops the task; on Telegram that is every message
dropped.why: Confirmed broken, and already proposed. service/src/14-chats.mjs:208 clears the task on any owner message without reading it. It runs before the typed-yes path (:218-225), and conv.task is set nowhere else but :371, so a typed yes also ends the work. Telegram has one rolling chat (21-telegram.mjs:250-262, :272), so every Telegram message during work ends it. The fix is already in 04-wrong-as-wired-report.md:16 ('clear the task only on a new change request') and 01-gap-analysis-plan.md:42 (keep it through a typed yes). Neither is built; build that, with wake-1. The brain-sharing half is over-engineered. The gateway cap is for apps and its comment says the console's own chats are not counted (15-routes.mjs:181-183). A carry-on already runs under the owner's 4-slot limit (14-chats.mjs:183-184). The one-at-a-time setup at config.json:86-87 is one preset, not shown to be the running one.

missing.title: Can the brain itself do the change loop? Nobody measured it
missing.question: All 14 areas ask whether Sparkie has the tools to change itself; none asks whether Qwen can use them. The earlier plan parks self-change 'until the engine trial passes 2 of 3' (docs/analysis-2026-11-11/01-gap-analysis-plan.md:137), and /Users/akuppala/Documents/26aiRAG/spark-console/agentbar/ (run.mjs, grade.mjs, engines.mjs, tasks/, run-on-spark.sh) looks like that trial, yet it is absent from AGENTS.md, code-map.md and every finding. Find out: what agentbar tests, whether it was ever run against the current brain and with what score, and whether its tasks match this repo's real loop (edit a service/src part, write a test that fails first, build, run the closest test). Then measure the fit: the brain's context window and max_tokens (service/src/14-chats.mjs:255 uses 4096) against the biggest files (16-actions.mjs 79 KB, 17-changes.mjs 57 KB, public/app.js 343 KB) and the per-turn tool-round and 50-second action limits (14-chats.mjs:327). State the smallest pass bar the owner should require before retiring the Mac (for example three real past fixes replayed by Sparkie on the stand-in fleet), and what edit shape (whole-file, search/replace, line patch) a model of this size can do reliably.

missing.title: Work that outlives one turn: who wakes Sparkie when the hour-long gate ends
missing.question: A real change is edit, build, test, a one-hour gate, ask the owner, install, live check: many hours and many turns, across restarts (the install itself restarts the console) and past the 200-message wall. Findings cover multi-step stalls (brain-chat-2), a gate record, and approvals that survive, but nobody traced the whole chain. Trace in service/src/14-chats.mjs, 07-jobs.mjs and 18-workflows.mjs: when a long job finishes, what starts Sparkie's next turn (the carry-on path), how many carry-ons are allowed, what Sparkie knows at that point about the plan it was following, and what is left after a console restart or a brain restart mid-task. Say whether one small durable 'work in hand' record (goal, steps done, next step, files touched; read into each turn, cleared on done) is enough, and how it differs from the resume and problems.json ideas the learning area cut. Also say what the owner's chat does meanwhile, since one brain serves both the long task and the owner.

missing.title: Spark 2 cold boot and host upkeep after the Mac is gone
missing.question: Healing was traced for Spark 3/4 power cycles and a stopped brain, not for the hub itself. Trace a power cut on Spark 2 end to end, read-only from the code and installers: is linger on (deploy/host-on-portal.sh:198-199 only prints a note), does Docker bring the brain back (13-main-model.mjs:128 unless-stopped), do the Tailscale serve and Funnel settings from deploy/lock-api.sh and open-to-internet.sh persist, do the watchdog timer and Telegram loop restart, and how long is the owner without chat while the brain loads. Then list the host upkeep Claude or the owner does today that nothing does after handoff, and which of it the fixed rules forbid Sparkie to do: DGX OS and Docker and NVIDIA runtime updates (does unattended-upgrades run, can it restart Docker or break the GPU runtime under a running model), Node version, PyYAML (11-setups.mjs:27), journald and Docker image and Hugging Face cache growth on all three Sparks, chat and audit file growth in the state folder, and Tailscale key expiry (01-gap-analysis-plan.md:149 says 'by hand'; is it done, and is it sensed). For each: sense only, tell the owner with one command to paste, or leave alone.

missing.title: When Sparkie is stuck: no path is named, and no cloud model is allowed
missing.question: The fixed rules forbid a fallback brain or cloud escalation, and the plan forbids an agent or a patch starting an update (01-gap-analysis-plan.md:78). So what happens when Qwen fails the same fix three times, or the console is too broken for chat? Nobody traced it. Find out what exists today: does any counter stop repeated failed attempts, what does Sparkie say, and can the owner still reach a working state with only the owner words, undo_update and the recovery card. Then design the smallest honest exit that breaks no rule: Sparkie stops, says plainly it could not, and leaves one readable bundle (what was asked, what it tried, gate record, crash record, diff against the installed build) that the owner may hand to any helper they choose. Check whether the owner's own outside agent can already do the repair through the agent door (service/src/20-mcp.mjs, tools/spark.mjs) under the owner's approval, or whether the 'never an agent' guard makes a console that Qwen cannot fix unrecoverable without a terminal and deploy/host-on-portal.sh from a Mac. Say which scripts in deploy/ and tools/ still assume a Mac (power-setup.sh, lock-api.sh, open-to-internet.sh, cutover.sh all say 'run it from your Mac').

missing.title: Secrets and planted text once Sparkie can read files, logs, source and state
missing.question: Many kept findings give Sparkie new reads: files actions (ow-1), its own source and docs (brain-3, cd-1), crash and fault records, the audit (state-add-6), longer container logs (ow-7), a script runner (ow-6), web reads (02-tools-and-freshness.md:185). The access area checked doors, not what flows through the brain. Find out: which of these reads can return secrets.json, access.json, passkeys.json, agent keys, the Telegram token, the Hugging Face token (11-setups.mjs:395-396) or recovery codes; where such text would then land (chats.json, Telegram messages via 20-tell.mjs and 21-telegram.mjs, memory.json, the daily copy on Spark 3/4, an agent's ask_sparkie reply); and whether one masking rule at the action boundary exists or is needed. Second, trace planted instructions: text in a container log, a model card, a recipe file or a web page that tells Sparkie to remember a line, save a workflow, or propose a console change. Check ctx.readOutside (14-chats.mjs:354) covers every new read kind and that an owner approval shows the real diff, not the brain's summary of it.

missing.title: Time-based work: 'every night', 'at 7', 'in two hours' has no home
missing.question: The owner's goal is all workloads 'even simple ones', and the coding agent today has scheduled tasks. The earlier plan parked schedules 'until a real request' (01-gap-analysis-plan.md:138), and install B watches (docs/analysis-2026-11-11/09-telegram-design.md, channels-add-1) are event watches. Find out whether the watches design can carry a time trigger at no new machinery: one saved workflow name plus a time, run by the existing timer loop in service/src/25-backup-and-start.mjs or 19-watcher.mjs, result sent by 20-tell.mjs. Trace what must be true first: the saved-workflow run path with no chat attached (learning-3 says a step that asks ends the run), a missed run while the console or Spark 3/4 was off, the pause switch, and the rule that nothing starts on Spark 2. Give the smallest shape (for example at most 10 schedules, owner-only, listed in /status) or say plainly it should stay parked and why.

missing.title: Two kinds of work on one Spark's memory: who decides, and what the owner is told
missing.question: Serving was reviewed for models and other-workloads for services, each alone. Nobody traced them together on Spark 3 or 4, where memory is shared between GPU and system. Find out in service/src/05-library.mjs, 08-cluster.mjs, 17-changes.mjs and 19-watcher.mjs: does where_it_fits and start_model count memory held by non-model containers (ComfyUI, a notebook, a fine-tune or batch job, an embedding server), does a hand-started or Sparkie-started workload get stopped to make room for a model or the reverse, what does 'protected' cover, and what happens to the planned keep_running and run_script when a model start needs the room. Also check the two-Spark case: a pair start while a service holds memory on one side. State the one rule to write down (who yields, and that the owner is asked before anything not started by this request is stopped) and the test on the stand-in fleet that would prove it (tests-add-6 makes the stand-in docker generic).

missing.title: The handoff itself: what still lives only on the Mac, and the drill that proves the Mac can go
missing.question: Each area lists fixes; nobody owns the cutover. Make the inventory of what exists only on the Mac today: the source tree (not a git repo; the plan wanted a tagged git checkout on Spark 2, 01-gap-analysis-plan.md:73), Claude's memory notes beyond the fixed rules (fleet facts, 'hands off' rules, model-per-task habits), the owner's agent keys and tools/console.mjs sign-in, tools/build-catalog.py inputs, agentbar results, the scratchpad drafts, and any step in docs/retire-portal.md or docs/sharing.md that says 'from your Mac'. Then write the exit test as a short list of drills run by talking to Sparkie only, with the Mac closed: a comment-only change through gate, approval and install; a crash-at-start put back; a brain restart from Telegram; a model start, stop and diagnose on Spark 3/4; a state restore from the daily copy; sign-in recovery with a paper code. Say which drills are impossible today and name the single finding that blocks each.

mustChange: Prove the brain can write code now, not in Batch 10. The engine trial has never been run (no /Users/akuppala/Documents/26aiRAG/spark-console/agentbar/results folder), and the real-brain eval only has a partial result (test/eval/results-2026-11-08-partial.json). Make the trial measure the loop that ships. agentbar tests opencode and Qwen Code inside a container on Spark 3 or 4 (agentbar/README.md:3-9, 'not Spark 2: the trial's containers are workloads'). Milestone 7 describes something else: search-and-replace edits on a git branch on Spark 2 inside the console. Pick one and say it. If it is the in-console loop, the trial must drive that loop. If it is an engine in a container, self-change only works while Spark 3 or 4 is on, and the plan must say so.

Add the missing groundwork on Spark 2 to Batch 1. There is no git anywhere (the tree is not a repository; docs/reviews-2026-11-11.md:51), yet sticky item 13 and milestone 7 assume `.git`. If (b), the engine trial does not prove it; the trial must run that same loop.

Git is assumed but does not exist. The Mac tree is not a git repository, the source tar carries no .git (host-on-portal.sh:58-59), and the swap replaces ~/spark-console-src whole (:228-232). Either add an explicit one-time `git init` and first commit on Spark 2 as a named step (and check git is installed there), or drop git: work in a copied folder and build the change report with diff -ru. The second is smaller and has no new dependency.

The brain keeper as written will fight the owner. The brain runs with --restart unless-stopped (13-main-model.mjs:128), so Docker already brings back a crashed brain. An exited brain therefore almost always means someone stopped it: the page, the console's own failed switch, or the owner by hand on Spark 2 (the only way the owner swaps brains). stoppedByOwner in main.json cannot see a by-hand stop.
